domande.domanda: A project manager is asked by a senior manager to slightly misstate the project status in a report so that it appears healthier than it is. What should the project manager do?

opzioni.A: Decline and report the project status accurately and honestly.
opzioni.B: Comply since the request came from a senior manager.
opzioni.C: Misstate the status but note the truth informally to the team.
opzioni.D: Report the status as healthy.

domande.hint: Ethics: always tell the truth, even if it costs you your job.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Correct. Decline and report the status accurately and honestly.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Complying means lying to the stakeholders.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. You'd still be lying to the stakeholders.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Reporting the status as healthy is a lie.

domande.spiegazione: Ethics: always tell the truth, even if it costs you your job. B, C and D all mean lying to the stakeholders.

domande.domanda: A project manager leads a project where the sponsor wants frequent, detailed updates while the development team finds the reporting burden is cutting into its delivery time. What should the project manager do?

opzioni.A: Side with the team and reduce all reporting to the sponsor.
opzioni.B: Find a reporting approach that informs the sponsor with less burden on the team.
opzioni.C: Require the team to complete the reports on top of their work.
opzioni.D: Tell the sponsor that detailed updates are not possible.

domande.hint: Never take one side: find a solution that works for both.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Don't side with one party; the sponsor's need is legitimate.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. Tailor the reporting so the sponsor is informed with less burden on the team.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Pushing the team doesn't solve the problem.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. It does nothing for the sponsor.

domande.spiegazione: Never choose one side over the other: find a solution that works for both. Communication should be tailored to the stakeholder. C pushes people and D does nothing.

domande.domanda: ⚠️ A project manager leads a distributed team and notices that team cohesion is weak, with members rarely collaborating beyond their assigned tasks. What should the project manager do? — ⚠️ Note: options/text partly reconstructed from the transcript.

opzioni.A: Create opportunities for team members to build relationships and collaborate.
opzioni.B: Accept the lack of cohesion since the team is distributed.
opzioni.C: Require members to collaborate by formally mandating it.
opzioni.D: Reduce the size of the team.

domande.hint: Pick the answer that directly addresses the problem.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Correct. Create opportunities to build relationships and collaborate: it directly addresses weak cohesion.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Accepting it means doing nothing.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Mandating collaboration is pushing people.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Reducing the team means firing people.

domande.spiegazione: Pick the answer that directly addresses the problem. B does nothing, C pushes people, D fires people.
domande.nota: Option D reconstructed ('reduce the team').
domande.motivo_incertezza: options/text partly reconstructed from the transcript

domande.domanda: A project manager leads a project where stakeholders keep requesting small changes that seem minor but collectively are expanding the scope. What should the project manager do?

opzioni.A: Approve small changes individually to keep stakeholders happy.
opzioni.B: Reject all small changes.
opzioni.C: Route every change through change control to assess the cumulative impact.
opzioni.D: Implement the changes and update the baselines afterwards.

domande.hint: This is scope creep on a traditional project.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. No change should be approved just like that.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Rejecting changes is not within the PM's power.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. Route every change through change control to assess its cumulative impact.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Changes must be assessed and approved before baselines are updated.

domande.spiegazione: This is scope creep: no change is approved just like that, and rejecting isn't within the PM's power. Changes are assessed and approved before baselines are updated.

domande.domanda: ⚠️ A project manager managing a contract notices that the supplier's deliverables, while on time, have begun slipping in quality. What should the project manager do? — ⚠️ Note: options/text partly reconstructed from the transcript.

opzioni.A: Withhold all payments until the quality improves.
opzioni.B: Terminate the contract.
opzioni.C: Continue accepting the deliverables to maintain the schedule.
opzioni.D: Discuss the quality concern with the supplier against the contract terms.

domande.hint: Meet, confront the problem and solve it against the contract.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Withholding payment is like holding someone to ransom.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Terminating is too drastic as a first step.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Accepting declining quality is doing nothing.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Correct. Discuss the quality concern with the supplier against the contract terms.

domande.spiegazione: Meet, confront the problem and solve it. Withholding payment is like holding someone to ransom; terminate/stop are drastic; accepting as is does nothing.
domande.nota: Option C reconstructed (unclear transcript).
domande.motivo_incertezza: options/text partly reconstructed from the transcript

domande.domanda: A team member tells the project manager that another team member has been taking credit for the first member's work, creating tension on the team. What should the project manager do?

opzioni.A: Publicly clarify who did the work during the next meeting.
opzioni.B: Speak with both team members to understand and resolve the issue.
opzioni.C: Ignore it.
opzioni.D: Reassign one of the members.

domande.hint: Tension between people is resolved privately, with the people involved.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Never resolve tension between individuals in public.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. Speak with both team members privately to understand and resolve the issue.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Ignoring it is kicking the can down the road.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Don't fire or reassign people as a first step.

domande.spiegazione: Resolve tension privately, with the people involved. Never in public, never ignore it, never fire or reassign people as a first step. Expect many questions like this on the exam.

domande.domanda: A project manager leads a project in which a deliverable failed a quality test late in execution, and the cost to fix it is now higher than it would have been earlier. What should the project manager do to prevent this?

opzioni.A: Increase the budget to absorb the late fixes.
opzioni.B: Wait until final testing to catch all defects at once.
opzioni.C: Build quality checks into the process earlier.
opzioni.D: Assign quality responsibility entirely to a separate team.

domande.hint: The keyword is 'prevent': the answer must be something done earlier.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Increasing the budget is reactive (and needs a change request).
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Waiting lets problems grow and costs more.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. Build quality checks into the process earlier to catch defects when they're cheap to fix.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. A separate quality team doesn't prevent late defects.

domande.spiegazione: The keyword is 'prevent': the answer must be something done in the past/earlier. A is reactive; B lets problems progress; D doesn't help. Build quality in early.

domande.domanda: Midway through a sprint, a developer realizes that a user story already completed in the current sprint would deliver significantly more value with a small enhancement. What should the project manager do next?

opzioni.A: Add the enhancement to the current sprint so the value is captured immediately.
opzioni.B: Raise the enhancement during the next retrospective.
opzioni.C: Add the enhancement as a backlog item for the product owner to prioritize.
opzioni.D: Discuss the enhancement at the next daily stand-up.

domande.hint: Any new work goes through the product owner.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Nice in real life, but it breaks agile rules: sprint scope doesn't change mid-sprint.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Waiting until the retrospective delays it needlessly.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. Add it as a backlog item for the product owner to prioritize (or reject).
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. The stand-up is only for the three questions.

domande.spiegazione: Any work goes through the product owner, who may also reject it. A breaks agile rules; waiting for the retrospective is slow; the stand-up is only for the three questions.

domande.domanda: ⚠️ During execution, a stakeholder raises a concern that might develop into a problem later but cannot be acted on at this time. In which document should the project manager record the concern? — ⚠️ Note: options/text partly reconstructed from the transcript.

opzioni.A: Risk register
opzioni.B: Issue log
opzioni.C: Assumption log
opzioni.D: Change log

domande.hint: Has it happened, or might it happen?

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Correct. Something that might happen is a risk: record it in the risk register.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Issues are things that have already happened.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. It isn't an assumption.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Nothing needs to change in the plan yet.

domande.spiegazione: It's something that might happen, so it's a risk. Issues are things that have already happened; it isn't an assumption, and nothing needs to change the plan.
domande.nota: Options C and D reconstructed: only A and B are clear in the video.
domande.motivo_incertezza: options/text partly reconstructed from the transcript

domande.domanda: A new regulation takes effect next quarter and the project must be compliant before completion. What should the project manager do next?

opzioni.A: Assess the impact and process the requirements through integrated change control.
opzioni.B: Inform the product owner that the project will continue as planned.
opzioni.C: Add the new requirement directly to the scope baseline.
opzioni.D: Notify the steering committee of the new constraint.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Correct. Assess the regulation's impact and process the requirement through integrated change control.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Continuing as planned ignores the regulation.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Nothing goes into the baseline without assessment and change control.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Assess the impact before notifying anyone.

domande.spiegazione: For anything compliance-related, assess how the regulation affects the project before acting. Don't ignore it, don't add it to the baseline without change control, and assess before notifying.

domande.domanda: A project is in its final phase when a key stakeholder requests a change that would extend the critical path by two weeks. What should the project manager do?

opzioni.A: Reject the change.
opzioni.B: Apply schedule compression to absorb the additional change.
opzioni.C: Perform a detailed impact analysis before responding.
opzioni.D: Initiate the corresponding response from the risk register.

domande.hint: Extending the critical path moves the project end date.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. The PM can't simply reject a change.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Compression may come later, after the analysis.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. Perform a detailed impact analysis before responding (then maybe compress).
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. A change request is not a risk.

domande.spiegazione: Extending the critical path extends the project end date. The PM can't simply reject; compression may come later; a change request is not a risk. Do C, then maybe B.

domande.domanda: A client complains that a delivered component is not working. The project manager investigates and finds that the component had been outsourced to an external provider, which the project manager was never aware of. Which tool would primarily have helped the project manager identify the situation earlier?

opzioni.A: Risk register
opzioni.B: Communications management plan
opzioni.C: Procurement management plan
opzioni.D: Stakeholder register

domande.hint: The external provider is someone affected by the project that the PM never identified.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. It's not a risk scenario.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Nothing indicates a communication failure.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. The procurement management plan says how to manage procurement, not what is procured (that's the procurement SOW).
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Correct. The provider is a stakeholder that should have been identified in the stakeholder register.

domande.spiegazione: The external provider is a stakeholder the PM didn't identify. The procurement management plan says how to manage procurement, not what is procured (that's the procurement statement of work).

domande.domanda: ⚠️ A project team is midway through building a logistics platform, and the lead engineer proposes swapping the planned database technology for a newer one she believes will perform better. Several team members are persuaded by her track record of sound technical calls. The team's willingness to follow her lead is best explained by which form of power? — ⚠️ Note: options/text partly reconstructed from the transcript.

opzioni.A: Expert power
opzioni.B: Legitimate power
opzioni.C: Reward power
opzioni.D: Coercive power

domande.hint: Why do they follow her? Look at 'track record of sound technical calls'.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Correct. Following someone because of their knowledge and track record is expert power.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Legitimate power is 'do it because I'm the manager/lead'.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Reward power is bonuses, days off or recommendations in exchange for compliance.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Coercive power is threats ('or I'll fire you'), the worst power to use.

domande.spiegazione: They follow her because of her track record of sound technical calls: expert power. Legitimate power is 'do it because I'm the manager'; reward power is bonuses or recommendations; coercive power is threats ('or I'll fire you'), the worst power to use.
domande.nota: Option D (coercive) inferred from the comment on the 'worst power'.
domande.motivo_incertezza: options/text partly reconstructed from the transcript

domande.domanda: A team is struggling to follow newly implemented organizational standards after a company-wide transformation. As a result, leadership is questioning whether the project should continue. What should the project manager do first?

opzioni.A: Identify the team's skill gaps and provide the training and support needed to meet the new standards.
opzioni.B: Meet with the executive to clarify how the new standards affect project priorities.
opzioni.C: Keep the project focused on the original plan while documenting issues caused by the organizational change.
opzioni.D: Ask the sponsor to explain the new organizational expectations to the project team.

domande.hint: What is the root cause stated in the question?

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Correct. The team struggles with the new standards: identify skill gaps and provide training and support.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Second best, but it concerns project priorities, not the team's struggle.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Sticking to the original plan doesn't solve anything.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. The organization's expectation is simply to get the project done; the issue is the team's skills.

domande.spiegazione: The root cause is that the team struggles with the standards, so train them. B is second best but concerns project priorities, not the team; C does nothing; the organization's expectation is simply to get the project done. Pick the answer that directly answers the question.

domande.domanda: ⚠️ An agile team is developing 80 user stories across 4 iterations. Each completed user story is valued at $40, so the project budget is $3,200. At the end of the second iteration the team has completed 40 user stories and spent $1,400. What is the status of the project? — ⚠️ Note: options/text partly reconstructed from the transcript.

opzioni.A: The project is under budget and ahead of schedule.
opzioni.B: The project is over budget and on schedule.
opzioni.C: The project is under budget and on schedule.
opzioni.D: The project is on budget and behind schedule.

domande.hint: 80 stories / 4 iterations = 20 per iteration. Compare planned vs completed and earned vs spent.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Under budget is right, but 40 stories after 2 iterations is exactly on schedule, not ahead.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Earned value is 40 x $40 = $1,600 and only $1,400 was spent: under budget.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. 40 stories planned and 40 done = on schedule; $1,600 earned vs $1,400 spent = under budget.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Spending is below earned value (not on budget) and the schedule is on track (not behind).

domande.spiegazione: 20 stories per iteration means 40 stories should be done after two iterations: on schedule. 40 x $40 = $1,600 should have been spent but only $1,400 was: under budget.
domande.nota: Options B and D reconstructed from the commentary (only A and C are clear in the video).
domande.motivo_incertezza: options/text partly reconstructed from the transcript

domande.domanda: A project manager has been assigned to a newly approved project. While reviewing the project documentation, the project manager cannot determine how the expected business outcome supports the organization's strategic goals. What should the project manager do first?

opzioni.A: Begin project planning because the project has already been approved.
opzioni.B: Revise the business case to better align the project.
opzioni.C: Perform a risk assessment to determine the impact of the uncertainty.
opzioni.D: Meet with the sponsor to clarify how the project supports the organizational strategy.

domande.hint: Before planning, understand how the project creates value for the organization's strategy.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Planning matters, but first understand the value the work is meant to deliver.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. The project is approved: your job is to understand the business case, not change it.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Useful later, but understand the value first.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Correct. Meet the sponsor, who approved the project, to clarify how it supports the strategy.

domande.spiegazione: First understand how the project adds value to the organization's strategy; the sponsor approved it. You don't change an approved business case; planning and risk assessment come after (C, B or A).

domande.domanda: A project is three weeks behind. The project manager runs an AI scheduling tool that analyzes dependencies and resource availability and recommends resequencing several activities to recover the time. The tool can apply the new schedule automatically once accepted, and the sponsor wants the recovery plan in place by the end of the day. What should the project manager do?

opzioni.A: Reject the AI recommendation and have the team rebuild the recovery schedule manually to be safe.
opzioni.B: Review the AI sequencing for errors, then allow the tool to apply the new schedule automatically.
opzioni.C: Analyze the AI recommendation with the team and make the final decision on the schedule change.
opzioni.D: Forward the AI recommendation to the sponsor for approval.

domande.hint: AI assists, humans decide: validate AI output before accepting it.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Rejecting the tool entirely wastes it; welcome the tool, but validate it.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Letting the tool apply changes automatically trusts AI too much.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. Analyze the recommendation with the team and make the final, human decision.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. The sponsor isn't the right person to judge the schedule detail; that's your job.

domande.spiegazione: AI assists, humans decide: validate AI output before accepting it. A rejects the tool entirely; B trusts AI too much; the sponsor isn't the right person to judge it, that's your job.

domande.domanda: ⚠️ A key stakeholder asks the project manager to add a new deliverable to a predictive project that is already in execution, citing a shift in business priority. What should the project manager do? — ⚠️ Note: options/text partly reconstructed from the transcript.

opzioni.A: Add the deliverable to the project scope since the stakeholder holds considerable influence over the project's success and reputation.
opzioni.B: Inform the stakeholder that changes are not accepted once execution has begun.
opzioni.C: Submit the request through the change control process to assess its impact before proceeding.
opzioni.D: Note the request in the issue log and revisit it at closure.

domande.hint: Predictive project in execution: how is every change handled?

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Influence doesn't skip assessment and approval.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Never deny a change outright.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. Submit it through change control to assess the impact before proceeding.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Nothing negative has happened, so it's not an issue; and don't wait until closure.

domande.spiegazione: On a predictive project every change goes through change control: assess first, then get approval. Never deny a change; nothing negative has happened yet, so it isn't an issue.
domande.nota: Option D reconstructed (unclear transcript).
domande.motivo_incertezza: options/text partly reconstructed from the transcript

domande.domanda: Midway through a construction project, a new environmental regulation requires additional sustainability reporting that was not part of the original compliance plan. What should the project manager do?

opzioni.A: Determine the new compliance requirements and assess their impact on the project scope and schedule.
opzioni.B: Continue current operations since the compliance plan was already approved at initiation.
opzioni.C: Escalate the regulation change to legal counsel and pause all project activities until a ruling is issued.
opzioni.D: Assume the operations team will independently manage the new requirements.

domande.hint: Law and compliance must be followed: what do you need to know first?

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Correct. Determine the new requirements and assess their impact on scope and schedule.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. A new regulation must be followed; the old approval doesn't cover it.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Legal may come later, but pausing everything is too drastic.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Never assume; the PM must be involved.

domande.spiegazione: When there's a law or compliance requirement, you must follow it and know how it affects the project. B ignores it; C may come later but stopping everything is too much; never assume.

domande.domanda: ⚠️ A senior stakeholder asks a developer to add an urgent feature directly to the current sprint work. The developer has not started the feature and the product owner has not evaluated its value or priority. What should the project manager do? — ⚠️ Note: options/text partly reconstructed from the transcript.

opzioni.A: Allow the feature because development has not started.
opzioni.B: Ask the team to estimate the feature immediately.
opzioni.C: Direct the stakeholder to submit the request to the product owner.
opzioni.D: Have the developer add the feature to the sprint backlog because it is urgent.

domande.hint: Product owner controls the product backlog; the team controls the sprint backlog.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Don't allow it just because work hasn't started; it hasn't been evaluated.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Don't go to the team first; beware of words like 'immediately'.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. The stakeholder must take the request to the product owner, who evaluates and prioritizes it.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Urgency doesn't bypass the product owner; the sprint backlog belongs to the team.

domande.spiegazione: The product owner controls the product backlog (adds, prioritizes, removes); the team controls the sprint backlog. Beware words like 'immediately' or 'must'.
domande.nota: Option D is not read in the source video: it was written as a plausible distractor. Answer C is from the source.
domande.motivo_incertezza: options/text partly reconstructed from the transcript

domande.domanda: A hybrid project team used an unapproved AI tool to summarize confidential stakeholder comments. The summary remains internal, but organizational policy requires approved tools and provides an escalation path for possible data exposure. What should the project manager do first?

opzioni.A: Assess the compliance impact and follow the escalation path.
opzioni.B: Delete the summary and recreate it using an approved tool.
opzioni.C: Inform every stakeholder that a confirmed data breach occurred.
opzioni.D: Allow temporary use of the tool until the governance team reviews it.

domande.hint: Follow the organizational policy: it tells you what to do.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Correct. Assess the compliance impact and follow the escalation path defined by policy.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Decent, but don't throw away work the team may need before assessing.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. No breach has been confirmed.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Continuing to use the tool goes against policy.

domande.spiegazione: Understand the impact and follow the escalation path defined in organizational policy. B throws away work the team may need; no breach is confirmed (C); D allows something against policy. With AI: don't trust it, always review the output, and remember the PM is accountable.

domande.domanda: An agile team has missed its sprint goal in three consecutive sprints. Velocity has remained stable, but unfinished work is repeatedly carried forward because acceptance criteria are interpreted differently by developers and testers. What should the project manager do?

opzioni.A: Increase the sprint length to give the team more testing time.
opzioni.B: Facilitate agreement on the acceptance criteria and the definition of done.
opzioni.C: Ask the product owner to reduce the number of backlog items.
opzioni.D: Assign a senior tester to approve all completed stories.

domande.hint: The problem is interpretation, not the amount of work.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. A longer sprint doesn't fix the different interpretations.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. Bring people together to agree on acceptance criteria and the definition of done.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Reducing backlog items reduces value.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Only the customer accepts the work, not a tester.

domande.spiegazione: The problem is a misinterpretation of the acceptance criteria, not the amount of work: bring people together to agree. A doesn't fix it; C reduces value; only the customer can accept the work, not a tester.

domande.domanda: A predictive project depends on a supplier delivering a custom component. The first shipment arrives three days late, but schedule analysis confirms the available float absorbs the delay. The contract requires escalation after a five-day delay, and no previous delays have occurred. What should the project manager do?

opzioni.A: Rebaseline the schedule to reflect the supplier's actual performance.
opzioni.B: Escalate the delay because future delays may follow.
opzioni.C: Monitor the supplier's performance against the contract and schedule.
opzioni.D: Replace the supplier.

domande.hint: Float absorbs the delay and the contract threshold hasn't been reached.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. The float absorbs the delay: no rebaseline needed.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. The contract requires escalation after 5 days; it's 3, and it's the first delay.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. Monitor the supplier against the contract and schedule (and talk to them).
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Replacing the supplier is drastic.

domande.spiegazione: Float (time an activity can slip without delaying the project) absorbs the delay, so just monitor and talk to the supplier. No rebaseline, no escalation, no drastic action like replacing the supplier.

domande.domanda: An agile team receives updated usage data showing that three planned features have low expected customer value. The product owner has not yet reviewed the data and the next sprint has not started. Developers propose removing the features during backlog refinement. What should the project manager do?

opzioni.A: Facilitate a backlog reprioritization with the product owner using the updated value data.
opzioni.B: Allow developers to remove the features.
opzioni.C: Escalate the value concern to the sponsor before changing anything.
opzioni.D: Focus the next sprint on the originally planned features to preserve the plan.

domande.hint: Who can remove or reprioritize product backlog items?

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Correct. Facilitate reprioritization with the product owner using the new value data.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Developers can give input but can't remove backlog items.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. It's the product owner's job, not the sponsor's.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Ignoring the warning keeps low-value work in the plan.

domande.spiegazione: Only the product owner can add, remove and reprioritize backlog items; developers can only give input. It's the product owner's job, not the sponsor's, and the warning shouldn't be ignored.

domande.domanda: Customer feedback shows that a partially developed feature provides little value. The product owner wants to continue because the team has already spent significant time building it. What should the project manager do?

opzioni.A: Complete the feature to recover the team's previous investment.
opzioni.B: Escalate the product owner's decision directly to the sponsor.
opzioni.C: Re-evaluate the feature using current feedback and expected value.
opzioni.D: Remove the feature without consulting the product owner or stakeholders.

domande.hint: Sunk cost is no reason to continue: projects exist to create value.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Finishing low-value work just because time was spent is the sunk cost fallacy.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. That's between sponsor and product owner; don't escalate first.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. Re-evaluate the feature using current feedback and expected value.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. You have no authority to remove it without the product owner.

domande.spiegazione: A project exists to create value; if the work doesn't add value, don't do it (sunk cost is no reason to continue). Re-evaluate with current feedback. That decision sits between the sponsor and the product owner, and you have no authority to remove the feature on your own.

domande.domanda: ⚠️ An agile team is halfway through a sprint when a senior executive bypasses the product owner and requests a new feature. The team immediately begins working on it, which will prevent them from achieving the current sprint goal. What should the project manager do now? — ⚠️ Note: options/text partly reconstructed from the transcript.

opzioni.A: Direct the team to stop work and refer the executive to the product owner.
opzioni.B: Update the sprint backlog to include the executive's feature.
opzioni.C: Arrange a meeting between the steering committee and the project team.
opzioni.D: Allow the team to complete the feature to maintain the executive's goodwill.

domande.hint: Exam answer, not real-life: once the sprint starts, protect the sprint goal.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Correct. Stop the off-goal work and send the executive to the product owner, who manages the product backlog.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. The team, not the PM, updates the sprint backlog, and the sprint goal shouldn't change.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. This belongs between the executive and the product owner, not the team.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Probably what happens in real life, but it breaks agile rules.

domande.spiegazione: Not the real-life answer but the exam answer: once the sprint starts, don't change the sprint goal or the team. The executive goes to the product owner, who adds items to the product backlog; the team, not the PM, updates the sprint backlog.
domande.nota: Option D reconstructed (truncated transcript).
domande.motivo_incertezza: options/text partly reconstructed from the transcript

domande.domanda: A vocal stakeholder repeatedly pushes the product owner to prioritize a set of niche features. Adoption data from the last two releases confirm that fewer than 5 percent of users engage with these features. The value components of the product were agreed by all stakeholders at project kickoff. What should the project manager do?

opzioni.A: Escalate the stakeholder's influence over the backlog to the sponsor.
opzioni.B: Facilitate a workshop with all stakeholders to redefine the project's value components.
opzioni.C: Review the adoption data with the product owner to support value-based reprioritization.
opzioni.D: Direct the team to pull only high-value items into the next sprint.

domande.hint: Two good answers: which comes first?

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. The backlog belongs to the product owner, not the sponsor.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. First facilitate a workshop with all stakeholders to redefine value, then reprioritize with the product owner.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Good, but second, after the value definition is realigned.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. The team already pulls high-value items; that's not the problem.

domande.spiegazione: B and C are both good mindset answers: do B first (workshop to redefine value), then work with the product owner to reprioritize. A belongs to the product owner, not the sponsor; D isn't the problem, since the team already pulls high-value items.

domande.domanda: An agile project manager at a healthcare software company notices that during the last three daily stand-ups, two senior developers have openly dismissed a junior tester's impediments, telling her to just figure it out. The junior tester has now stopped speaking, and a defect she was blocked on has slipped into the sprint's final week. What should the project manager do first?

opzioni.A: Raise the behavior in the next retrospective so the whole team can address it together.
opzioni.B: Speak privately with the two senior developers to understand the situation and address the behavior.
opzioni.C: Escalate the interpersonal conflict to the functional managers of the two developers.
opzioni.D: Re-establish the team ground rules at the next sprint planning session.

domande.hint: Problems with one or a few people are handled privately and now.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Waiting for the retrospective kicks the can down the road while the sprint suffers.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. Speak privately with the two developers to understand and address the behavior.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Escalating gives away your problem.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Waiting for the next sprint delays it, and ground rules are set by the team.

domande.spiegazione: Never kick the can down the road (A, D wait until the sprint ends) and never give away your problem (C). Tip: with problems involving one or a few people, always speak to them privately, never in front of the team.

domande.domanda: The project manager on a pharmaceutical validation project learns that a functional manager has reassigned the lead validation engineer to an urgent product recall for the next four weeks. The engineer's validation activities are on the critical path and no one else on the team holds the required certification. What should the project manager do first?

opzioni.A: Escalate the resource conflict to the sponsor for resolution.
opzioni.B: Meet with the functional manager to explain the project's impact and negotiate options.
opzioni.C: Update the schedule baseline to reflect the four-week delay.
opzioni.D: Begin certifying another team member to take over the validation.

domande.hint: Meet people and look for a solution before escalating or re-planning.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Escalation may come later, not first.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. Meet the functional manager, explain the impact and negotiate options.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. You may update the baseline later, but not first.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Certifying someone takes a long time: last resort.

domande.spiegazione: Meet people and try to find a solution first. Escalation may come later; updating the baseline you'd probably do later too; certifying someone else takes a lot of time and is the last resort.

domande.domanda: During a site walk on a mural restoration project, an apprentice points out that the paint supplier occasionally back-orders one pigment. What should the project manager do first?

opzioni.A: Add this to the issue log.
opzioni.B: Note the risk in the risk register and make the team aware of it.
opzioni.C: Tell the apprentice the risk is too minor to bother tracking.
opzioni.D: Book a risk workshop to analyze the pigment supply in depth.

domande.hint: It hasn't happened yet: risk or issue? And which step comes first?

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. It hasn't happened, so it's not an issue.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. Record it in the risk register and inform the team; analyze it afterwards.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. All risks should be tracked.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Analysis is right but comes after registering the risk.

domande.spiegazione: It hasn't happened yet, so it's a risk, not an issue. Track all risks. Analyzing (D) is also right but comes after: first register it and inform the team, then analyze in a workshop.

domande.domanda: A hotel rebrand project has closed and the project manager has just finished the final lessons-learned meeting. What should the project manager do next?

opzioni.A: Send the lessons learned to every employee in a company-wide email.
opzioni.B: Store the meeting notes in the closed project's own archive folder.
opzioni.C: Forward the results to the project management office so they can share them with other projects.
opzioni.D: Hold a celebration to mark the team's accomplishment.

domande.hint: How do lessons learned reach other projects?

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. A company-wide email to everyone isn't the right channel.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Archiving is also done, but hiding it there doesn't let others learn.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. Send the lessons learned to the PMO so they can be shared with other projects.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Celebrating is nice, but not the next step.

domande.spiegazione: Update the lessons learned register and give it to the PMO, which distributes it to all other projects. B is also needed but hiding it in the archive doesn't let others learn; A and D are not right.

domande.domanda: A project manager is running a web platform build when a normally reliable senior engineer begins missing deliverable dates, which will soon affect the go-live date. What should the project manager do next?

opzioni.A: Meet with the engineer privately to understand their concerns and any issues.
opzioni.B: Meet with the whole team to discuss the misses and their impact on the go-live.
opzioni.C: Document the misses in the issue log and monitor for another sprint.
opzioni.D: Notify the engineer's functional manager and ask if there are known problems.

domande.hint: Keyword 'next': who do you talk to first?

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Correct. Meet the engineer privately first to understand what's happening.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Possibly afterwards, but first speak with the individual.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Monitoring for another sprint delays the fix.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Don't report people; solve the problem yourself.

domande.spiegazione: A and B are both meeting-based; the keyword is 'next/first': meet the person, understand why, then maybe the whole team. C waits another sprint; D reports a person instead of solving the problem.

domande.domanda: ⚠️ At project kickoff the whole team agreed on core working hours. Months later one team member says those hours no longer work because of new family obligations. What should the project manager do? — ⚠️ Note: options/text partly reconstructed from the transcript.

opzioni.A: Meet one-on-one with the team member to negotiate a personal schedule adjustment.
opzioni.B: Reassess the working hours collaboratively with the whole team.
opzioni.C: Ask the team member to adjust their personal commitments.
opzioni.D: Refer the matter to HR.

domande.hint: Who agreed on the working hours in the first place?

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Tempting, but the hours were agreed by the whole team, so a one-on-one deal isn't enough.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. Reassess the working hours collaboratively with the whole team.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Never push someone to give up personal or family obligations.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Referring to HR gives away your problem.

domande.spiegazione: A difficult one. Never push someone away from personal or health issues (C) and never give away your problem (D). The key: the whole team agreed on the hours, so a change must be reassessed with the whole team, not negotiated one-on-one.
domande.nota: Text of options C and D reconstructed (fragmented transcript).
domande.motivo_incertezza: options/text partly reconstructed from the transcript

domande.domanda: ⚠️ A mining project signed contracts for heavy machinery and site services. Mid-execution, the machinery supplier announces it cannot deliver, and there is no time to source a new supplier without delaying the project. What should the project manager do first? — ⚠️ Note: debatable: the instructor sees more than one valid answer.

opzioni.A: Review the existing site services contract for an option that can help supply the machinery.
opzioni.B: Review the market for alternative machinery suppliers and begin a new procurement process.
opzioni.C: Add the shortfall to the risk register and wait for the supplier to confirm a new date.
opzioni.D: Buy the machinery from another supplier and inform change control.

domande.hint: Read the constraint: there is no time to source a new supplier.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Correct. Check whether the existing site services contract can help supply the machinery. Not perfect, but the best of the four.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. The question says there's no time for a new supplier.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. The supplier cannot deliver: it's an issue, not a risk, and waiting does nothing.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Again, no time for a new supplier.

domande.spiegazione: The statement says there is no time to source a new supplier, ruling out B and D; the supplier says it cannot deliver, so it's an issue, not a risk (C). A is not the greatest answer but the best of the four.
domande.nota: The instructor: 'not the best answer in absolute terms, but the best of these four'.
domande.motivo_incertezza: debatable: the instructor sees more than one valid answer

domande.domanda: A fintech startup is launching a payment product with a fixed regulatory deadline. In the first planning session, the team sees that the requirement list is far too large to deliver by that date. What should the project manager do first?

opzioni.A: Ask the product owner to remove the lowest priority item until the list fits the date.
opzioni.B: Fast-track the schedule by running design and build activities in parallel.
opzioni.C: Onboard contract developers to increase delivery capacity immediately.
opzioni.D: Ask the team to propose a minimum viable product that can meet the date.

domande.hint: When MVP is an option, it may well be the best answer.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Removing items blindly is a last resort.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Fast-tracking forces the team when it has said the date isn't feasible.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Adding contractors changes the whole setup.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Correct. Have the team propose an MVP: functional, quick, without every feature, that meets the date.

domande.spiegazione: A minimum viable product is quick and functional without every feature. Don't just remove items (A), don't force the team (B), don't change the whole setup (C). Tip: when MVP is a choice, it may well be the best answer.

domande.domanda: A project manager leading a large agile project communicated ground rules to the team at the start. Around the 10th iteration, several team members have clearly stopped following them. What should the project manager do first to restore adherence to the ground rules?

opzioni.A: Ask a functional manager to replace the members who are not complying.
opzioni.B: Add the violations to each member's next performance evaluation.
opzioni.C: Schedule a meeting with the team to revisit and reinforce the ground rules.
opzioni.D: Meet individually with each member who is not following the ground rules.

domande.hint: 'Several' members on a 'large' project: individually or as a team?

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Replacing people before trying to fix the problem is drastic.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Punishing comes before trying to solve the problem.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. With several members involved, revisit and reinforce the ground rules with the team.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Good in general, but many one-on-ones on a large project is less sensible.

domande.spiegazione: C and D are both good, but 'several' team members on a large project means a team meeting is more sensible than many one-to-one meetings. A fires people and B punishes them before trying to solve the problem.

domande.domanda: A vendor building a claims processing system tells the project manager one week before user acceptance testing that only half of the promised functionality will be ready by the UAT start date. What should the project manager do next?

opzioni.A: Adjust the schedule to match the vendor's current progress.
opzioni.B: Communicate with the vendor and the team to explore options to resolve the issue.
opzioni.C: Meet with the vendor to renegotiate the delivery milestones in the contract.
opzioni.D: Notify legal counsel.

domande.hint: Work with the vendor and the team before changes, contracts or lawyers.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. You can't just adjust the schedule; it needs a change request.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. Communicate with the vendor and the team to explore options.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Renegotiating may come later, not first.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Don't bring in lawyers yet.

domande.spiegazione: Work with the team and the vendor first. You can't just adjust the schedule (it needs a change request); renegotiating milestones or bringing in lawyers comes later, if at all.

domande.domanda: The sponsor tells the project manager that a key stakeholder complains the reported metrics make the project look out of control. The project manager has followed the agreed communications management plan, but this stakeholder rarely attends the status meetings. What should the project manager do first?

opzioni.A: Send the sponsor proof that all reports were distributed per the agreed plan.
opzioni.B: Meet with the stakeholder to walk them through the current metrics and clear up the confusion.
opzioni.C: Ask the sponsor to require the stakeholder's attendance at future status meetings.
opzioni.D: Evaluate the communication needs, identify the gaps and adjust the plan if needed.

domande.hint: The plan was followed, yet the stakeholder is confused: is the plan right for them?

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Proves you followed the plan, but doesn't fix the stakeholder's confusion.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Good, but it only fixes this instance; the communication may not fit this stakeholder's needs.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Not everyone needs to attend status meetings.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Correct. Evaluate the stakeholder's communication needs, find the gaps and adjust the plan.

domande.spiegazione: B is good, but D is better: maybe the metrics or the meetings aren't what this stakeholder needs, so adapt the communication to the stakeholder's needs. A only proves you followed the plan; not everybody has to attend status meetings.

domande.domanda: Acting as a servant leader on an agile pilot, a project manager sees the team demo the product after three sprints and receive negative stakeholder feedback, even though every feature met the product owner's acceptance criteria. The team is confused about what went wrong. How should the project manager mitigate further product rejections?

opzioni.A: Share the product backlog with the main stakeholders and review it before each sprint.
opzioni.B: Ask the product owner to rewrite the acceptance criteria with more detail.
opzioni.C: Engage the main stakeholders directly in the upcoming sprint review sessions.
opzioni.D: Schedule dedicated sprints to rework the rejected feature.

domande.hint: 'Mitigate further rejections': prevent, don't fix the past.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. The product backlog is controlled by the product owner.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. The features already met the criteria; that's not the problem.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. Engage the main stakeholders in every sprint review so feedback comes early.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Rejected work goes back to the backlog; this fixes the past, it doesn't prevent.

domande.spiegazione: Meeting the acceptance criteria doesn't mean people will like it: stakeholders should be involved in every sprint review, not only after the third. A: the backlog belongs to the product owner; B isn't the issue; D fixes the past, doesn't prevent it (rejected work goes back to the backlog).

domande.domanda: A project spread across several international offices is trending late. The project manager discovers that key activities were scheduled during national holiday periods at the overseas locations. What should the project manager do next?

opzioni.A: Update the schedule to reflect the holidays and distribute the workload across offices to limit slippage.
opzioni.B: Insert a schedule buffer after each holiday period to absorb the delay.
opzioni.C: Update the schedule to reflect the holidays and inform the sponsor that the completion date will move.
opzioni.D: Ask the overseas offices to work through the holidays.

domande.hint: Never make people work holidays; then try to limit slippage before moving dates.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Correct. Update the schedule for the holidays and redistribute the workload to limit slippage.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Buffers don't fix activities scheduled on holidays.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Good, but second: if slippage can't be limited, then inform the sponsor.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Never ask people to work through their national holidays.

domande.spiegazione: Never go against someone's culture and never make people work holidays or overtime. A and C are both good: first limit the slippage (A); if that doesn't work, then inform the sponsor of the new date (C).

domande.domanda: ⚠️ While reviewing progress on a logistics project, the project manager notices that a previously identified risk has now materialized into an issue. What should the project manager do to address the situation? — ⚠️ Note: answer letter inferred from the commentary.

opzioni.A: Submit a change request to draw additional funds from the management reserve.
opzioni.B: Collaborate with the team to brainstorm response options for the issue.
opzioni.C: Move the item from the risk register to the issue log and continue monitoring.
opzioni.D: Collaborate with the relevant stakeholders on implementing the planned risk response.

domande.hint: The risk was previously identified: a response should already exist.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Don't draw on reserves right away.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. No need to brainstorm: a planned response already exists.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Monitoring isn't enough: you must act.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Correct. Implement the planned risk response from the risk register with the stakeholders involved.

domande.spiegazione: The risk was previously identified, so a response is already planned in the risk register: execute it. Don't brainstorm again, don't just keep monitoring, and don't draw on reserves right away.
domande.nota: Letter D inferred from the commentary (the instructor doesn't say it).

domande.domanda: ⚠️ During execution of a hospital construction project, a key supplier goes bankrupt and cannot deliver the contracted materials, which could affect the schedule. What should the project manager do first? — ⚠️ Note: options/text partly reconstructed from the transcript.

opzioni.A: Escalate to the management team to obtain approval for a delay.
opzioni.B: Update the issue log and act to minimize the impact on the project.
opzioni.C: Freeze all related work packages until a replacement is found.
opzioni.D: Update the risk register and develop a mitigation plan.

domande.hint: The supplier has already gone bankrupt.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Escalating for a delay isn't the first step.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. It's an issue: update the issue log and act to minimize the impact.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Don't freeze work yet.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. It would be the risk register only if it 'could' go bankrupt.

domande.spiegazione: The supplier has already gone bankrupt, so it's an issue, not a risk: update the issue log and minimize the impact. If it said 'could go bankrupt' it would be the risk register (D). Don't freeze work yet; escalation isn't the first thing.
domande.nota: Option D reconstructed (truncated transcript).

domande.domanda: A project manager runs a global project where dispersed stakeholders interpret requirements differently, raising concerns about scope creep as many people ask for changes throughout the project. What action should the project manager take to control the scope?

opzioni.A: Accept only changes that clearly add measurable value to the project.
opzioni.B: Freeze the requirements document after sign-off and defer all changes to a phase 2.
opzioni.C: Accept only changes that have been approved by the change control board before implementation.
opzioni.D: Obtain agreement from all stakeholders that no changes will be needed.

domande.hint: Traditional project: how are changes controlled?

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Many changes add value; that alone isn't enough to accept them.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Freezing and deferring everything means rejecting changes.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. Only changes approved by the CCB are implemented.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Expecting no changes is unrealistic.

domande.spiegazione: On a traditional project, changes go through the change control process: if approved by the board, implement. Don't accept changes just because they seem valuable, don't reject everything, and don't expect no changes.

domande.domanda: A medtech company completed a limited pilot release of a diagnostic platform that it now intends to deploy in multiple countries. Stakeholders have raised concerns about different international health regulations and the associated risks. What should the project manager do next?

opzioni.A: Review the compliance and regulatory requirements together with the stakeholders.
opzioni.B: Review lessons learned from similar multi-country deployments before proceeding.
opzioni.C: Delegate regulatory review to each country's own sales team.
opzioni.D: Pause the rollout until a single global regulatory standard can be confirmed.

domande.hint: Two good answers: who knows the regulations right now?

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Correct. Review the compliance and regulatory requirements with the stakeholders first.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Good, but second, after understanding the regulations with the stakeholders.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Sales teams can't help with regulatory review.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. A single global standard is unlikely; don't pause.

domande.spiegazione: A and B are both good; do A first: meet the stakeholders to understand the regulations and how they affect the project, then learn from similar deployments. Sales teams can't help; a single global standard is unlikely.

domande.domanda: Midway through a two-week sprint, the team loses confidence in the increment it is building and wants product owner validation now instead of waiting for the sprint review. What should the project manager do to mitigate this risk?

opzioni.A: Extend the sprint end date.
opzioni.B: Schedule an additional interim demo with the product owner.
opzioni.C: Tell the team to raise the concern at the next retrospective.
opzioni.D: Invite the product owner to the daily stand-ups.

domande.hint: Serve the team: give it what it needs, within agile rules.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. The team, not the PM, decides sprint length.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. Schedule an extra interim demo with the product owner to validate the increment.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Telling them to wait ignores the team's need.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. The stand-up is for the team; inviting the product owner goes against agile rules.

domande.spiegazione: Serve the team: give them what they want. The team (not the PM) decides sprint length; telling them to wait ignores them; the stand-up is for the team, so the product owner shouldn't attend it (against agile rules).

domande.domanda: On a distributed team, a developer keeps delaying a coding task that sits on the critical path. The project manager learns the delay stems from the developer's confusion about requirements written by the offsite analyst. What should the project manager do?

opzioni.A: Meet with the developer to coach them on implementing the requirements documentation.
opzioni.B: Replace the developer with a more experienced resource.
opzioni.C: Facilitate communication between the developer and the offsite analyst to clarify the requirements.
opzioni.D: Ask the offsite analyst to reassign the task to someone in their own location.

domande.hint: When there's confusion, it's your job to clear it up.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Coaching on technical requirements isn't the PM's role.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Don't replace people.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. Facilitate communication between the developer and the analyst to clarify the requirements.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Don't take work away from people.

domande.spiegazione: When there's confusion it's your job to clear it up: connect the two people. Coaching on interpreting requirements is technical, not the PM's role; don't fire or take away people's jobs.

domande.domanda: A project manager joins a technical research project whose team is already staffed. The lead subject matter expert sends over a list of technical skills the project will require. What should the project manager do next?

opzioni.A: Meet with the subject matter expert to validate the list and prioritize which skills matter most.
opzioni.B: Benchmark the list against similar past projects before taking action.
opzioni.C: Forward the list to the team and instruct them to obtain training on the required skills.
opzioni.D: Meet with the team to understand their skills and identify gaps and training.

domande.hint: Two good answers: what must you know first?

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Good, but second: first know where the team's gaps are.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Benchmarking questions the SME's expertise.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Telling them to get training leaves them on their own.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Correct. Meet the team to understand their skills and identify gaps and training needs.

domande.spiegazione: A and D are both good: first find out whether the team can do these things and where the skill gaps are (D), then go back to the SME with the gaps. B questions the SME; C leaves people alone.

domande.domanda: ⚠️ Halfway through a project, the sponsor is replaced by a peer who had no prior involvement. The new sponsor rejects most project artifacts, the latest increment goes unapproved and stakeholder confidence drops. What should the project manager have done? — ⚠️ Note: options/text partly reconstructed from the transcript.

opzioni.A: Ask the departing sponsor to formally pre-approve the remaining increments.
opzioni.B: Perform a stakeholder analysis as soon as the new sponsor joined the project to understand how that person wants to be communicated with.
opzioni.C: Escalate immediately to ensure the deliverables would be approved.
opzioni.D: Hold a one-on-one onboarding session to brief the new sponsor on the project's history.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. You can't pre-approve increments that don't exist yet.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. Analyze every new stakeholder as soon as they join and tailor communications.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Escalating is corrective, not preventive.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. An onboarding on project history alone isn't enough.

domande.spiegazione: The key word is 'should have': prevention. Whenever a new stakeholder joins, analyze them and update the communication needs. Escalating is corrective, not preventive; the onboarding session isn't enough on its own.

domande.domanda: A pharmaceutical product is planned across eight fixed-date iterations. At the start of iteration 2, the project manager discovers that a significant regulatory feature is missing from the product backlog. What should the project manager do?

opzioni.A: Ask the product owner to add the missing feature to the backlog.
opzioni.B: Log the omission as a quality defect.
opzioni.C: Convince the stakeholders to assess the impact of adding the regulatory feature.
opzioni.D: Insert the feature directly into the iteration.

domande.hint: 'Iterations' means agile. Who owns the product backlog?

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Correct. The product owner owns the product backlog: ask them to add the missing feature.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Nothing says it's a quality defect.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Assessing the impact is your job, with the product owner.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Only the product owner adds features; the team manages the iteration.

domande.spiegazione: 'Iterations' signals an agile project. The product owner is in charge of the product backlog and no one else should add to it; the team manages what gets done inside the iteration. It's your job (with the product owner) to assess the impact, and it's not known to be a defect.

domande.domanda: ⚠️ An agile coach and a technical writer sit nine time zones away from the rest of the delivery team. The team lead wants to hold the daily coordination meeting (the daily stand-up) at 10:00 AM local time, but the remote pair say that time is unworkable for them. How should the project lead ensure adherence to agile practices? — ⚠️ Note: options/text partly reconstructed from the transcript.

opzioni.A: Meet with the remote pair separately to find a time acceptable to them.
opzioni.B: Alternate the daily coordination meeting time weekly.
opzioni.C: Have a discussion with the whole team and decide together when the daily coordination meeting should be.
opzioni.D: Record each daily coordination meeting and have the remote pair post asynchronous updates.

domande.hint: Let the team work out its problems; you coordinate.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. It leaves out the lead and the rest of the team.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. A compromise that doesn't help anyone.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. Discuss with the whole team and decide together.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. The remote pair would no longer really be involved.

domande.spiegazione: Let the team work out its own problems while you coordinate. A leaves the lead and the rest of the team out; B is a compromise that doesn't help anyone; D means the remote pair are not actually involved.
domande.nota: Final sentence of the question reconstructed (unclear transcript).
domande.motivo_incertezza: options/text partly reconstructed from the transcript

domande.domanda: A project manager contracted a vendor to build a new inventory system. During acceptance testing, the delivered system quality is clearly unsatisfactory. How should the project manager support the claim to the vendor?

opzioni.A: Provide the failed test results together with the agreed-upon acceptance criteria.
opzioni.B: Provide a detailed defect log compiled by the testing team during acceptance testing.
opzioni.C: Send the vendor a demand letter stating industry quality benchmarks.
opzioni.D: Submit a customer satisfaction survey showing users' negative reactions.

domande.hint: What is the strongest proof the contract wasn't met?

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Correct. Failed test results against the agreed acceptance criteria are the strongest proof.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Good, but less conclusive than failed tests against the criteria.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. A demand letter on industry benchmarks doesn't prove a contract breach.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. A satisfaction survey doesn't prove the acceptance criteria weren't met.

domande.spiegazione: The goal is to prove the system is unsatisfactory: the failed tests against the agreed acceptance criteria are the strongest proof. B is also good but less conclusive; a demand letter or a survey doesn't show the contract wasn't met.

domande.domanda: A team has started using an AI-based estimation tool trained on historical project data relevant to the upcoming release. The tool's estimates are significantly lower than what the experienced team members believe is realistic. What should the project manager do?

opzioni.A: Adopt the AI estimates since they are based on objective historical data rather than opinion.
opzioni.B: Facilitate a session where the team compares the AI output against their expert judgment and agree on the estimates.
opzioni.C: Discard the tool output and rely solely on the team.
opzioni.D: Ask the vendor to retrain the AI model before the team commits to any estimates.

domande.hint: Don't blindly trust AI, but don't discard it either.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Never blindly trust AI over experienced people.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. Compare AI output with expert judgment and agree on the estimates together.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Don't give up on the tool.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. It's already trained on historical data; retraining isn't the point.

domande.spiegazione: Exam tip: don't blindly trust AI. AI assists and we must always verify its output before using it. Don't discard the tool either; and the model is already trained on historical data, so retraining isn't the point.

domande.domanda: A consistently strong performer on a data migration project has recently shown a performance drop and has become short-tempered with colleagues in meetings. The project manager has worked with this person for months and has never seen this behavior. What should the project manager do?

opzioni.A: Attend more team meetings to observe this individual closely and determine the root cause.
opzioni.B: Discuss the observations privately with the individual to understand why this is happening.
opzioni.C: Ask other team members whether they have noticed the behavior.
opzioni.D: Raise the performance drop with the individual's functional manager and human resources.

domande.hint: A one-person problem is handled with that person, privately.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Observing lets the behavior continue.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. Discuss privately with the individual to understand why.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Asking others gives away your problem.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Don't report people; deal with them directly.

domande.spiegazione: Never choose an answer that kicks the can down the road (A). With a problem involving one person, address it with that person individually. Don't give away your problem, and don't report or snitch on people (C, D). A very common PMP question.

domande.domanda: A capital project depends on shared resources from the company's contracts department. During execution, contracting work for the project keeps slipping, and the project manager learns that the department deprioritizes the work because they don't feel part of the project team. What should the project manager do first?

opzioni.A: Escalate to senior management and ask them to direct the contracts department to prioritize the project.
opzioni.B: Schedule a recurring meeting with the contracts department to press them on the project's critical deadlines.
opzioni.C: Ask the contracts manager to formally commit dedicated hours.
opzioni.D: Meet with the contracts department to build trust and commitment by recognizing their critical role.

domande.hint: The real cause: they don't feel part of the team.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Senior management isn't there to solve your problems.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Pressing people is not servant leadership.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Not bad, but it pushes them instead of engaging them.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Correct. Build trust and commitment by recognizing their critical role.

domande.spiegazione: Solve the real problem: they don't feel part of the team. Senior management isn't there to solve your problems; don't push people, encourage them (servant leader, not dictator).

domande.domanda: ⚠️ A team wrote user stories after gathering customer requirements, but as delivery progresses, change requests keep piling up and the team feels its output does not match what the customer actually wants. What should the project manager do? — ⚠️ Note: options/text partly reconstructed from the transcript.

opzioni.A: Arrange a workshop with the customer to understand the business value expected from the outcomes.
opzioni.B: Search the configuration management knowledge base for similar past projects to reuse requirements.
opzioni.C: Ask the customer to designate a representative to co-locate and work alongside the team.
opzioni.D: Hire additional senior team members to improve the quality of the work.

domande.hint: Who can tell you whether the work has value?

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Correct. A workshop with the customer clarifies the business value expected.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Past requirements won't satisfy this customer.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Not bad, but less direct than understanding value from the customer.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Nothing says the team is weak.

domande.spiegazione: The team doesn't know whether what it builds has value for the customer: the best person to tell you is the one you make it for. Reusing past requirements doesn't satisfy this customer; nothing says the team is bad.
domande.nota: Option D reconstructed (fragmented transcript); C is a good alternative but less direct.
domande.motivo_incertezza: options/text partly reconstructed from the transcript

domande.domanda: A newly appointed project manager for a fully remote team rolled out the AI collaboration toolset that had worked well on the previous project. Several team members are unhappy with the choice. What should the project manager have done to avoid this?

opzioni.A: Delegate the tool selection to the project's technical lead.
opzioni.B: Let the team members use whichever tool works best for them individually.
opzioni.C: Meet with the project team to determine their collaboration needs and identify the tools that fit them.
opzioni.D: Pilot the previous toolset for one iteration before committing to it.

domande.hint: 'Should have done': prevention. Who should choose the tools?

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. It hands the decision to one person.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Individual tool choices hurt collaboration.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. Work with the team to determine collaboration needs and the tools that fit.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Still imposes the old tool.

domande.spiegazione: We're not fixing the problem, we're preventing it: every project is different and the team must choose its tools. It's servant leadership to support the team with what they need. A hands it to one person; B ignores the need to collaborate; D still imposes the old tool.

domande.domanda: ⚠️ Factory acceptance tests on a complex assembly revealed several deficiencies. Delivery of the assembly is on the critical path and any delay will push out the project completion. What should the project manager do? — ⚠️ Note: options/text partly reconstructed from the transcript.

opzioni.A: Hold the shipment at the vendor's facility until all rework is fully complete.
opzioni.B: Set up frequent status calls with the vendor to keep the rework visibility on track.
opzioni.C: Ship the unit as is and complete the corrective work on site.
opzioni.D: Assess the schedule impact and evaluate the most feasible option to keep the project on track.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Possibly needed, but first assess.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Possibly needed, but first assess.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Don't ship a failing product.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Correct. Assess the schedule impact and evaluate the most feasible option.

domande.spiegazione: A and B may both be needed, but first assess the schedule impact and evaluate the most feasible option. Don't ship a failing product (C).
domande.nota: Options C and D reconstructed from a fragmented transcript.
domande.motivo_incertezza: options/text partly reconstructed from the transcript

domande.domanda: A delivery team has been unable to complete an iteration successfully for several months. The recurring obstacle is that requirements enter the sprint unclear. What should the project leader do?

opzioni.A: Recommend limiting work in progress so the team can focus on fewer items.
opzioni.B: Recommend that the product owner review the product backlog refinement process.
opzioni.C: Recommend the team extend the iteration to allow more time for clarification.
opzioni.D: Recommend a review of individual team members' performance.

domande.hint: Who refines the backlog so requirements are clear before the sprint?

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. WIP limits address flow speed, not unclear requirements.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. The product owner owns backlog refinement.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Requirements should be clear before the iteration starts.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Nothing indicates individual performance problems.

domande.spiegazione: The product owner is in charge of refining the product backlog and breaking items down so the team understands them. WIP limits address speed, not unclear requirements; requirements should be clarified before the iteration; nothing says individuals have a problem.

domande.domanda: A project manager wants to use a generative AI assistant to draft status reports and stakeholder communications faster. Some of the project information involved is commercially sensitive, and the organization has begun defining rules for AI use. What should the project manager do first?

opzioni.A: Allow the team to use the AI assistant freely since it only drafts text that a human will review.
opzioni.B: Anonymize the sensitive details manually and begin using the assistant right away.
opzioni.C: Review the organization's AI and data governance policies and assess the confidentiality risk before adopting the tool.
opzioni.D: Prohibit any AI use on the project until the technology matures.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Freely using AI ignores the organization's rules.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Using it right away bypasses the policies.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. Review AI and data governance policies and assess confidentiality risk first.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Don't ban AI; use it in compliance.

domande.spiegazione: If rules or regulations exist, the project manager must follow them, not go around them. Don't stop using AI either: use it in compliance with organizational and country rules, policies and laws.

domande.domanda: ⚠️ A company reorganization is on the way, and several key members of a project in execution are likely to be moved off the team. What should the project manager do? — ⚠️ Note: options/text partly reconstructed from the transcript.

opzioni.A: Determine the impact to the project and implement the mitigation plan, updating the project management plan.
opzioni.B: Begin recruiting replacements immediately.
opzioni.C: Meet with the affected team members to reassure them and support their transition.
opzioni.D: Ask the sponsor to shield the team from the reorganization.

domande.hint: First understand the impact on the project.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Correct. Determine the impact and implement mitigation, updating the plan.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Don't recruit before knowing the impact.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Good, but second.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. The organization has decided; don't run to the sponsor.

domande.spiegazione: First know how it will affect the project: that's one of the primary duties of a project manager. Reassuring the team comes second; don't recruit before knowing the impact; the organization already decided and you shouldn't go to the sponsor to solve your problem.
domande.nota: Text of option A reconstructed (unclear transcript).
domande.motivo_incertezza: options/text partly reconstructed from the transcript

domande.domanda: ⚠️ A global team uses video conferencing for daily meetings, but only a handful of members ever speak, and misunderstandings have multiplied as a result. What should the project manager do to address this? — ⚠️ Note: options/text partly reconstructed from the transcript.

opzioni.A: Use round-robin check-ins during the meeting so every participant has the opportunity to speak.
opzioni.B: Book one-on-one calls with the quiet members to collect their updates separately.
opzioni.C: Appoint one representative to gather and share updates on behalf of the wider group.
opzioni.D: Review the team's ground rules to reconfirm the original participation agreement.

domande.hint: Get to the core of the problem.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Correct. Round-robin check-ins get everyone speaking in the meeting.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. One-on-ones keep them out of the meeting.
