domande.domanda: An agile team in your organization would like to include Feature-Driven Development (FDD) practices in its way of working. You tell them FDD activities are supported by a core set of software engineering best practices. Which practices will the team start with?

opzioni.A: Feature releases, feature celebrations and feature iterations.
opzioni.B: Developing by feature, working in feature teams, and visibility of progress and results.
opzioni.C: Finding features, developing features and testing features.
opzioni.D: Ensuring executive features are allocated and developed.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. It rolls off the tongue, but isn't FDD.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. FDD's core practices include developing by feature, feature teams, inspections, regular builds and visibility of progress (similar to XP).
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. 'Finding features' isn't an FDD practice.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. The product owner prioritizes features, not executives.

domande.spiegazione: FDD practices resemble XP.

domande.domanda: Your agile team has been using Feature-Driven Development (FDD) as a model for its way of working for some time and is ready to add more FDD practices. What can the team do next?

opzioni.A: Ask the product owner for more features in the backlog.
opzioni.B: Hold a retrospective together to gather ways to improve.
opzioni.C: Incorporate configuration management and individual class ownership.
opzioni.D: Send key representatives to the Scrum of Scrums across the organization.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. A standard agile practice, not specific to FDD.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Good agile practice, but not specific to FDD.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. These are FDD core engineering practices (along with the domain object model): tracking changes and assigning code classes to owners.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. A scaling practice, not specific to FDD.

domande.spiegazione: FDD core engineering practices.

domande.domanda: An executive in your organization approaches you about working in an agile team. They've heard about Feature-Driven Development (FDD) and would like to try it as a 'test and learn' in your team. What do they mean by this?

opzioni.A: Your team will rely on previous feature designs for its work.
opzioni.B: Your team features certain abilities and showcases them to other teams.
opzioni.C: Your team enjoys the feature of working with agile in an agile organization.
opzioni.D: Your team will trial developing an overall model, then planning, designing and building by feature.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Not FDD.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Contains the word 'feature', but isn't FDD.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Contains the word 'feature', but isn't FDD.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Correct. FDD starts with an overall model, then plans, designs and builds by feature; once a feature is complete, the process starts again with what was learned.

domande.spiegazione: FDD starts with an overall model.

domande.domanda: In Kanban (flow-based agile), the number of story cards in progress follows the work-in-progress (WIP) limit shown on the visual or virtual Kanban board. The team pulls cards from the backlog column based on its capacity. These story cards provide an increment of value and are a primary:

opzioni.A: Driver of executive behavior.
opzioni.B: Measure of progress.
opzioni.C: Way to pay for the cost of an agile team.
opzioni.D: Enabler of people's engagement.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Not related.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. The key to Kanban is making progress visible; visible progress also improves engagement and makes blockers clear.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Not related.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Tricky: progress does improve engagement, but Kanban is primarily a way of showing and measuring progress.

domande.spiegazione: Visible progress improves engagement.

domande.domanda: You've just come on board an agile team and a decision needs to be made about product requirements. The Scrum Master asks the team to show thumbs up, thumbs down or thumbs sideways. What does a thumb sideways mean?

opzioni.A: The team member doesn't mind about the decision either way.
opzioni.B: The team member has a concern or conflict that needs further discussion.
opzioni.C: The team member defers to the executive sponsor to decide.
opzioni.D: The decision is outside the team member's expertise, so they choose not to vote.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Sounds right, but agile's power is in discussion.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. A sideways thumb signals a concern to discuss further (like a score of 3 or less in fist of five).
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Others may have information the executive doesn't.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Everyone should have a voice.

domande.spiegazione: Same as fist of five ≤3.

domande.domanda: You're at the beginning of a new iteration, about to plan and decide what gets worked on in the upcoming sprint. You decide to invite all project stakeholders to the planning meeting. Why is it important that all stakeholders are involved in decision making?

opzioni.A: So you can keep an eye on what they're doing.
opzioni.B: So business representatives can report back to their managers on the project.
opzioni.C: So the team feels important with lots of stakeholders present.
opzioni.D: So project stakeholders don't reject a decision that wasn't theirs.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Not the agile reason.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. It may help, but it's not the main reason.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Not the reason.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Correct. People are more likely to reject decisions they had no part in; involvement gains buy-in and commitment.

domande.spiegazione: Ownership gains buy-in.

domande.domanda: You're in an agile team and notice it is different from other project areas you've worked in. The project manager tells you there are certain ways to ensure stakeholders stay engaged. What is he talking about?

opzioni.A: Removing any team member who is not engaged in the project.
opzioni.B: Giving any extra work to the better-engaged team members.
opzioni.C: Ensuring visibility, transparency and progress of the work through charts and information in the common team area.
opzioni.D: Offering a possible promotion to the most engaged team member at the end of the project.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Not the first choice: agile wants people to come along for the journey.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Everyone should be involved in the work.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. Visible progress through information radiators (Kanban board, burndown, backlog) maintains engagement.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Not part of an agile team.

domande.spiegazione: Visible progress engages.

domande.domanda: ⚠️ You've been identified as a stakeholder on an agile software development team. When you join the team stand-up, you're surprised there are only eight people on the team, even though the deliverable is quite large. Why is the team so small? — ⚠️ Note: options/text partly reconstructed from the transcript.

opzioni.A: The agile methodology is being trialed as a cross-discipline, self-forming team.
opzioni.B: One person was selected for each necessary role, and no more.
opzioni.C: Agile methods recommend a delivery team of 12 or fewer members.
opzioni.D: The organization couldn't find any more available resources.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Self-forming teams are desirable, but that's not why it's small.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. A team may need multiple developers or testers (but ideally one product owner).
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. Agile recommends 12 or fewer, typically 3-9, to keep communication channels few and information flowing quickly.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Team size is a deliberate agile choice, not a resourcing accident.

domande.spiegazione: Channels = n(n-1)/2.
domande.nota: Option D is not read in the source: written as a plausible distractor.
domande.motivo_incertezza: options/text partly reconstructed from the transcript

domande.domanda: As the lead on an agile project, you have carefully cultivated a team of T-shaped people. What is a T-shaped person?

opzioni.A: A person with flat knowledge up top and long knowledge down the bottom.
opzioni.B: A person with a wide range of general skills and one deep skill or knowledge area.
opzioni.C: A person with a wide range of leadership skills, as everyone should lead on an agile team.
opzioni.D: A person with more contacts in the management layers and a few contacts in the team layer.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Not the definition.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. A generalizing specialist: broad general skills plus one deep specialty. Agile teams are ideally made of these.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Everyone can lead, but that's not the T-shaped definition.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Not the definition.

domande.spiegazione: Agile teams are made of generalizing specialists.

domande.domanda: In 2001, a group of individuals representing the most widely used lightweight software development methodologies agreed on a common set of values and principles, which became known as the Agile Manifesto. In that manifesto, what did they value?

opzioni.A: Individuals and interactions over processes and tools.
opzioni.B: Executive reporting over bottom-up reporting.
opzioni.C: Scrum Masters over project managers.
opzioni.D: Doing the work over viewing the work.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Correct. This is one of the four core values of the Agile Manifesto.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Not a manifesto value.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. The name of the role doesn't matter; the function does.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Sounds nice, but isn't a manifesto value.

domande.spiegazione: Agile Manifesto (2001).

domande.domanda: You're planning the next iteration for your agile team as the agile lead. The team will select user stories from the prioritized release backlog, elaborate them and estimate the work needed for each. The number of stories selected is based on:

opzioni.A: What the Scrum Master says, as they know best.
opzioni.B: The team's velocity: the rate at which the team can complete work.
opzioni.C: The Feature-Driven Development model.
opzioni.D: What the team wants to work on, to ensure individuals work within their strengths.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. The Scrum Master facilitates discussion; they don't decide.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. Velocity is the average amount of work completed in previous iterations (points, cards, T-shirt sizes or another agreed unit).
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Not related.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. The product owner sets priorities; the amount is based on velocity.

domande.spiegazione: Velocity can be points, cards, T-shirt sizes.

domande.domanda: Your team is standing around a board with cards on it. Each person answers these questions in round-robin fashion: What did I complete since last time? What am I planning to complete between now and next time? Is anything blocking me? What is the team doing?

opzioni.A: A lunch and learn.
opzioni.B: A working group meeting.
opzioni.C: The daily stand-up.
opzioni.D: A retrospective.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Not a lunch and learn.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Working group meetings still happen in organizations, but this isn't one.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. The daily stand-up: around 15 minutes, round-robin, talking to the cards in flight on the Kanban board.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Retrospectives are important, but this isn't one.

domande.spiegazione: Daily stand-up.

domande.domanda: ⚠️ There are multiple project life cycles to choose from, depending on the type of project, environment, deliverable and stakeholders. You're working on a project that requires features of an overall product to be delivered on a regular basis. Which project life cycle will you choose? — ⚠️ Note: debatable: the instructor sees more than one valid answer.

opzioni.A: Waterfall.
opzioni.B: Agile.
opzioni.C: Iterative.
opzioni.D: Incremental.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Waterfall is one big-bang release.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. It also meets the criterion, but agile combines iterative and incremental: the strict answer is incremental.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Iterative also delivers in one big bang, after iterating with feedback.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Correct. An incremental life cycle delivers features (increments of value) regularly over the life of the project.

domande.spiegazione: PMI life cycles.
domande.nota: In the source the explanation says 'iterative', but the answer chosen and the commentary point to incremental (D).
domande.motivo_incertezza: debatable: the instructor sees more than one valid answer

domande.domanda: You're working as an agile project manager in a new team that isn't familiar with agile. The executives aren't comfortable using agile in full just yet, so you suggest a hybrid approach to begin with, to help the organization meet its goals. What does this mean?

opzioni.A: A tailored combination of predictive, iterative, incremental and agile approaches.
opzioni.B: Using a project management plan to plan the project while delivering in features.
opzioni.C: A combination of reactive and proactive approaches.
opzioni.D: Using agile only when it's needed, such as in a software development team.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Correct. A hybrid life cycle incorporates parts of predictive, iterative, incremental and agile, letting the PM tailor the approach to the situation.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Close, but only one specific combination: hybrid takes whatever pieces suit the situation.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Not the definition.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Agile principles apply beyond software development.

domande.spiegazione: Tailor the approach to the situation.

domande.domanda: The agile team leader practices servant leadership and has built a safe environment for disagreement. How has this empowered the team to move forward without obstacles?

opzioni.A: The team is able to create a list of reasons why tasks cannot be completed.
opzioni.B: The team has no conflict and gets along very well.
opzioni.C: The team leader takes responsibility for all decisions.
opzioni.D: The team is encouraged to participate in discussion and even disagreement, in order to make better decisions.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. The focus is on solving problems, not listing reasons.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. A little safe conflict is healthy and needed for problem solving.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Servant leaders let the team do its work.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Correct. Constructive disagreement surfaces risks and alternative ideas; it's only sustainable with high psychological safety.

domande.spiegazione: Needs high psychological safety.

domande.domanda: New project teams go through the Tuckman model of forming, storming, norming and performing. You've just taken the lead of a new project with a newly formed team, and you're surprised to find little conflict and that the forming stage has gone so quickly. Which of the following might be the reason?

opzioni.A: The team members have worked together on previous projects and are following the same agile ceremonies and methods.
opzioni.B: You've made all the project decisions yourself, so they don't have to worry.
opzioni.C: The team is in line for a promotion, so they really want to get along.
opzioni.D: The team members really care about the product being delivered.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Correct. Having worked together before and using the same ceremonies shortcuts the forming and storming stages.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Not the agile way.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Not the reason.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Important, but working together before is the main factor.

domande.spiegazione: Tuckman: forming, storming, norming, performing, adjourning.

domande.domanda: You're the project manager of a new agile project. You ask your team questions to elicit their needs and help them solve problems as they arise. Which role are you fulfilling in the agile team?

opzioni.A: Project director.
opzioni.B: Project coach.
opzioni.C: Project support.
opzioni.D: Project executive.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Agile leaders facilitate rather than direct.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. Whatever its name (Scrum Master, agile lead), the role is servant leadership: coaching the team, growing it and removing blockers.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Not this role.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. A sponsor or executive may exist, but that's not what you're doing.

domande.spiegazione: Project coach/Scrum master.

domande.domanda: You're an agile project manager leading a new software project. During the last retrospective there was very little engagement and feedback, and the team seems to be losing interest in their work. What will you do to improve the situation?

opzioni.A: Hold another retrospective to try to extract more information.
opzioni.B: Align the project goals with each team member's personal goals.
opzioni.C: Hold a vote on whether to continue the project or not.
opzioni.D: Get executive management involved so team members raise their engagement.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Doing the same thing would likely give the same result.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. Aligning project goals with personal goals and playing to strengths makes people care more and work harder.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. The project may simply have to continue.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Unlikely to raise engagement.

domande.spiegazione: Play to strengths.

domande.domanda: You're working as a project manager in a team that is moving to an agile way of working. Previously you engaged the team in a single weekly working group meeting, with email as the primary communication. What changes will you make in the new agile team?

opzioni.A: Ensure reports are created weekly for executive management.
opzioni.B: Set up a teleconference with the different parts of your project team.
opzioni.C: Co-locate the team where possible and focus on frequent face-to-face communication.
opzioni.D: Have frequent one-on-ones with your team members to get their points of view in private.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Too slow; agile prefers face-to-face communication.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. OK if people aren't in the same place, but there's a better option.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. Co-location enables face-to-face discussion and gaining information by osmosis (overhearing useful conversations).
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Can help, but agile prefers collaborating as a team.

domande.spiegazione: Osmotic communication.

domande.domanda: ⚠️ Kanban translates to 'visual sign' or 'card' in Japanese. It's a form of visual management taken from lean manufacturing (the Toyota Production System). What is it used for? — ⚠️ Note: options/text partly reconstructed from the transcript.

opzioni.A: Monitoring work in progress and enabling pull and flow.
opzioni.B: Enabling executive reporting.
opzioni.C: Measuring work velocity and elaborating story cards.
opzioni.D: Enabling team participation.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Correct. Kanban shows and limits work in progress; cards are pulled only when there's room, keeping work flowing.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Not its purpose.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Velocity is more Scrum; story elaboration involves the PO, BAs, developers and testers.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Not specifically Kanban's purpose.

domande.spiegazione: Kanban from Toyota Production System.
domande.nota: Options reconstructed from the commentary.
domande.motivo_incertezza: options/text partly reconstructed from the transcript

domande.domanda: You're working with an agile team that uses Kanban to manage the flow of work. The Scrum Master (agile lead) mentions the concept of 'pull', which helps the team manage the work. What does this mean?

opzioni.A: The team gathers around the team velocity board each morning to ensure the work is being done.
opzioni.B: The team pulls work only when they are ready.
opzioni.C: The team works with a pull-and-push approach between developers and testers.
opzioni.D: The Scrum Master tells the team to pull the appropriate levers that enable the right features to be developed.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. There's no 'velocity board' in this sense.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. New work is pulled onto the board when there's capacity; this limits WIP, encourages flow and makes blocked items visible so the team can swarm.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Right words, wrong idea.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Right words, wrong idea.

domande.spiegazione: Swarm blockers to keep flow.

domande.domanda: You're walking through the next feature with the product owner of an agile team. He is new to agile, unsure what Kanban really is, and lists a few things for you to check. Which of the following is NOT one of the core properties of Kanban?

opzioni.A: Visualize the workflow and limit work in progress.
opzioni.B: Manage flow and enable pull.
opzioni.C: Implement feedback loops and improve collaboratively.
opzioni.D: Follow procedures and don't deviate from the plan.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect: this IS a core property.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect: this IS a core property.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect: this IS a core property.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Correct: this is NOT a property. Kanban (from Lean/Toyota) limits WIP, keeps feedback loops and makes blockers visible.

domande.spiegazione: Kanban from Lean.

domande.domanda: You're working as an agile project manager and have been using Kanban to monitor the work and keep it visible for all to see. What is NOT a defining principle of Kanban?

opzioni.A: Start with the current state and respect the current process.
opzioni.B: Agree to pursue incremental, evolutionary change.
opzioni.C: Encourage leadership at all levels.
opzioni.D: Directive leadership over wasteful team participation.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect: this IS a Kanban principle.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect: this IS a Kanban principle.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect: this IS a Kanban principle.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Correct: this is NOT a principle. Kanban, like agile, encourages team participation over directive leadership.

domande.spiegazione: Kanban encourages participation.

domande.domanda: In 2001, a group of individuals representing the most widely used lightweight software development methodologies agreed on a common set of values and principles, which became known as the Agile Manifesto. Which of the following is one of the Agile Manifesto's core values?

opzioni.A: Directive leadership over servant leadership.
opzioni.B: Working software over comprehensive documentation.
opzioni.C: Making large, useful features over making small increments.
opzioni.D: Pushing work through quickly over limiting work in progress.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Agile prefers servant leadership.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. One of the four core values: release a working feature rather than writing a manual about it.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Agile releases small increments.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Agile limits work in progress.

domande.spiegazione: Agile Manifesto.

domande.domanda: You've joined a new project team that is moving to an agile way of working. Part of this is co-locating the team to gain the benefit of osmotic communication. Your project sponsor asks what this means. What do you tell them?

opzioni.A: The team is able to meet more frequently.
opzioni.B: It's easier to hand off work to someone if it meets their strengths.
opzioni.C: It's a written process made available to everyone in the team for transparency.
opzioni.D: The team will overhear conversations and information in the common area that will help them solve future problems.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. It helps, but that's not osmosis.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Agile actually wants to reduce handoffs.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Agile prefers interactions over processes.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Correct. Osmotic communication is the accidental overhearing of background information that may later be important.

domande.spiegazione: Benefit of co-location.

domande.domanda: You're working in an agile team that is not co-located: members are in various locations around the country. As the agile lead, how will you get the benefit of agile without a co-located team?

opzioni.A: Use group messaging, daily teleconference stand-ups, and an electronic Kanban board and backlog.
opzioni.B: Ask the organization to relocate the team.
opzioni.C: Hire or find new team members within the organization who are in the same place.
opzioni.D: Remove all meetings so people can focus on their work without distraction.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Correct. Moving or hiring whole teams may not be feasible; electronic tools for frequent contact are the most cost-effective approach.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Ideal, but rarely feasible.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. The skills you need may not be in one place.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Interaction is still needed.

domande.spiegazione: Use electronic tools.

domande.domanda: You're leading an agile team with members in various locations. You've arranged daily stand-ups by phone with an electronic Kanban board and backlog, but the team cannot meet face to face. What else will you do to help the team work together and get to know each other?

opzioni.A: Have a team board with their backgrounds and pictures.
opzioni.B: Swap roles throughout the team so each member gets a feel for what others do.
opzioni.C: Pair up team members to work on tasks and rotate the pairs for each feature.
opzioni.D: Hold a virtual lunch and learn where team members share something about themselves.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. It can help, but it's not the best agile option.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Agile prefers pairing up rather than swapping roles.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. Pair programming (from XP) works for most tasks and gives members the chance to talk and work one-on-one.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Pretty good, but working together on tasks is more effective.

domande.spiegazione: Pairing from XP.

domande.domanda: You're showing the project sponsor around the team area of your agile project, and you see the burndown chart next to the team's Kanban board. The project sponsor asks what the chart tells you. What will you say?

opzioni.A: It shows how many team members are moving on or off the project.
opzioni.B: It shows the remaining tasks versus what was planned for a given iteration.
opzioni.C: It shows the automated tests run as part of continuous integration.
opzioni.D: It shows the return on investment for delivered features.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Not what it shows.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. A line chart of tasks completed versus planned over the iteration; it can also track features over the project or risks, in any unit the team agrees.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Not what it shows.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Not what it shows.

domande.spiegazione: Can also track features or risks.

domande.domanda: You're working through the feature backlog with the organization's functional manager, who is also the product owner for your agile team. They ask about the velocity chart hanging in the team area. What do you tell them it is?

opzioni.A: The number of points, tasks or features completed by the team in each iteration.
opzioni.B: The number of team members working on the agile project.
opzioni.C: How fast each team member completes their work each day.
opzioni.D: The speed at which the project budget is being used up.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Correct. Velocity is the amount of work completed per iteration (often a planned vs. done bar chart); its average is used to plan future iterations.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Not velocity.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Velocity is a team measure, not per person.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Not a budget measure.

domande.spiegazione: Use average to plan iterations.

domande.domanda: ⚠️ In 2001, a group of individuals representing the most widely used lightweight software development methodologies agreed on a common set of values and principles, which became known as the Agile Manifesto. Which of the following is one of the manifesto's core values? — ⚠️ Note: options/text partly reconstructed from the transcript.

opzioni.A: Developer negotiation over customer demands.
opzioni.B: Product owner interaction over Scrum Master delegation.
opzioni.C: Customer collaboration over contract negotiation.
opzioni.D: Getting things right over getting the right things.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Agile avoids negotiation and responds to change.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Not a manifesto value.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. One of the four core values: collaborate with the customer instead of locking everything into a contract.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Both matter; it's not a manifesto value.

domande.spiegazione: Agile Manifesto.
domande.nota: Option A is only partially read in the source ('Developer negotiation'): its ending is reconstructed.
domande.motivo_incertezza: options/text partly reconstructed from the transcript

domande.domanda: You're working with your project team in a way that ensures you analyze the requirements, then design, build and test for those requirements, repeating them until the product is correct and adjusting your product or approach as necessary, before releasing it as one large feature. Which project life cycle are you using?

opzioni.A: Predictive.
opzioni.B: Agile.
opzioni.C: Incremental.
opzioni.D: Iterative.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Predictive plans upfront and doesn't change.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Agile also releases frequently.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Incremental releases small increments.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Correct. Iterative repeats analyze-design-build-test until correct, then delivers in one release.

domande.spiegazione: Agile = iterative + incremental.

domande.domanda: Large-Scale Scrum (LeSS) aims to organize several development teams toward a common goal by extending the Scrum method across teams. What is NOT one of the similarities between Large-Scale Scrum and normal Scrum?

opzioni.A: One single product backlog.
opzioni.B: One definition of done for all teams.
opzioni.C: Valuing individuals over results.
opzioni.D: One potentially shippable product increment at the end of each sprint.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect: this IS a similarity.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect: this IS a similarity.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct: this is NOT a similarity. Agile wants both individuals and results.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect: this IS a similarity. LeSS also has cross-functional teams and one product owner.

domande.spiegazione: Also cross-functional teams, one PO.

domande.domanda: Large-Scale Scrum (LeSS) aims to organize several development teams toward a common goal by extending Scrum across teams. Which of the techniques below was NOT added to Scrum to create LeSS?

opzioni.A: Sprint planning more formally divided into two parts: what and how.
opzioni.B: One single product release with no stakeholder feedback allowed.
opzioni.C: Overall cross-team refinement and organic cross-team coordination.
opzioni.D: An overall retrospective focused on cross-team improvements.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect: this WAS added.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct: this was NOT added. A single release is waterfall; agile depends on stakeholder feedback.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect: this WAS added.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect: this WAS added.

domande.spiegazione: LeSS scales Scrum.

domande.domanda: You're working on a project with clear procedures based on past projects. The product is clear and the risks are fairly well known, as the organization has done this before. Which of the following is true?

opzioni.A: It's definable work, so you can choose a predictive project life cycle.
opzioni.B: It's definable work, so you can choose agile.
opzioni.C: There's high uncertainty, so you can use incremental.
opzioni.D: There's high uncertainty, so you can use iterative.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Correct. With definable work and well-known risks, a predictive life cycle plans most of the project upfront with a single release.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Agile is for responding to change.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. The work isn't highly uncertain.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. The work isn't highly uncertain.

domande.spiegazione: Hybrid appears when risks pop up.

domande.domanda: You're an agile project manager leading a project team used to a waterfall way of working. The project sponsor wants to plan the entire project upfront so they can see when it will be delivered. You tell them agile uses adaptive planning. Why might this be a better alternative?

opzioni.A: Adaptive planning allows the project sponsor to adapt to the project plan over time.
opzioni.B: Adaptive planning allows the team to deliver usable features while continually reprioritizing the next pieces based on business value.
opzioni.C: Adaptive planning ensures users can adapt to the product.
opzioni.D: Adaptive planning is stable after the prototype is complete.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. The sponsor shouldn't have to adapt: the project serves their need for value.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. The sponsor receives incremental value as features, and the product owner reprioritizes throughout so the most valuable work comes next. (Many waterfall projects end up adaptive anyway.)
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. The product is built to deliver value to users, not the reverse.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Things keep changing once people get their hands on the product.

domande.spiegazione: Many waterfall projects end up adaptive.

domande.domanda: You're a Scrum Master about to begin a new iteration on your agile project. New features have been added to the backlog and the team is unsure which ones to work on next. How will you guide the product owner and the team when analyzing the next priority?

opzioni.A: Analyze the value of each feature with the product owner against the effort and the risk.
opzioni.B: Focus on the shortest tasks first so you can deliver quickly.
opzioni.C: Choose to deliver the entire project at the end.
opzioni.D: Ask the customers what they want delivered first.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Correct. The product owner prioritizes by weighing value against effort and risk; developing high-risk items early is just as important.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Not bad, but value versus effort and risk is better.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. That's waterfall.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. The product owner liaises with customers and owns the priority.

domande.spiegazione: PO prioritizes.

domande.domanda: You're coaching some team members who are new to agile, and someone asks what you mean by a 'time box'. What will you tell them?

opzioni.A: It is a period of time in which certain work is completed, such as an iteration.
opzioni.B: It is the time spent on a retrospective.
opzioni.C: It is the time taken to complete the project, with the 'box' representing the finished product.
opzioni.D: It is the effort assigned to a story card.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Correct. The classic time box is an iteration (usually around two weeks); spikes are time-boxed too. Time boxes counter Parkinson's law (work expands to fill the time available).
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Too narrow: a time box can apply to any work.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Clever, but not the definition.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. That's story points, which feed into velocity.

domande.spiegazione: Time boxes counter Parkinson's law.

domande.domanda: On your agile project team, you prioritize the backlog of features with the product owner and agree what to work on first. The project sponsor wants to know how long it will take to deliver some of this value. How will you estimate how long each feature will take to complete?

opzioni.A: Break the feature down into tasks or user stories, then estimate how long those will take with the development team.
opzioni.B: Take the total number of people in the team, multiply by the hours worked and divide by the number of features.
opzioni.C: Ask the project sponsor how many iterations the project is funded for, then plan to that.
opzioni.D: Find a similar feature delivered by another part of the organization and use that as the estimate.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Correct. Agile favors bottom-up estimating: work is broken down to user stories and estimated by the whole team doing the work.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Sounds complicated, but it isn't the right approach.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Happens in real life, but it's not estimating.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. That's analogous estimating: possible, but bottom-up gives the best view of the feature.

domande.spiegazione: Know three-point, analogous, parametric, bottom-up.

domande.domanda: You're working with an agile team on your first iteration. The product owner has chosen the feature and the team breaks it down into user stories to work on. What is a user story?

opzioni.A: A piece of functionality small enough to be completed in one to three days.
opzioni.B: A description of the feature from the viewpoint of the customer.
opzioni.C: A story about the end user, so the team understands the feature completely.
opzioni.D: A prioritized backlog.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Correct. A user story is the smallest unit of work; if it would take longer than one to three days, it's usually split into two or more pieces.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Pretty good, but it describes the acceptance criteria perspective more than the story itself.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Same as B.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. User stories make up the prioritized backlog.

domande.spiegazione: User stories.

domande.domanda: You've begun working on a project in a new organization, and the project team mentions you're working in an iterative project environment. How do you know you're working within an iterative project life cycle?

opzioni.A: The team iterates around one idea to make sure it's right.
opzioni.B: You're improving the product or result through successive prototypes or proofs of concept.
opzioni.C: The project sponsor says the project life cycle is iterative.
opzioni.D: You're using agile sprints or iterations to manage your work.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Uses the word 'iterate', but isn't the definition.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. An iterative life cycle uses successive prototypes or proofs of concept to gather feedback, then releases in one go.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Saying so doesn't make it so.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Using sprints doesn't make it an iterative life cycle.

domande.spiegazione: Iterative: feedback then one release.

domande.domanda: In 2001, a group of individuals representing the most widely used lightweight software development methodologies agreed on a common set of values and principles, which became known as the Agile Manifesto. Which of the following is one of the Agile Manifesto's core values?

opzioni.A: Developing as much as possible to see what gets the best result.
opzioni.B: Finding a product owner over finding a development team.
opzioni.C: Cross-functional team members over executive buy-in.
opzioni.D: Responding to change over following a plan.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Agile is about collaboration, feedback and change.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Both matter; not a manifesto value.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Both matter; not a manifesto value.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Correct. One of the four core values: following a plan still matters, but responding to change is valued more.

domande.spiegazione: Agile Manifesto.

domande.domanda: You're working on a project where the organization wants to move towards an agile way of working. Which two project life cycles combine to create an agile environment?

opzioni.A: Iterative and predictive.
opzioni.B: Incremental and predictive.
opzioni.C: Iterative and incremental.
opzioni.D: Predictive and agile.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Predictive is the waterfall approach.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Predictive is the waterfall approach.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. Agile combines incremental (smaller features released regularly) and iterative (improving through feedback).
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Predictive is not part of agile.

domande.spiegazione: Agile = iterative + incremental.

domande.domanda: You've come on board a new project team and been told the project works with a predictive style of project life cycle. How will you know you're working in a predictive (waterfall) approach?

opzioni.A: The bulk of the planning is done upfront and then executed in a single sequential process.
opzioni.B: The bulk of the planning is done upfront, then prototypes are created.
opzioni.C: A product roadmap is created, and smaller features are designed and released as part of the whole.
opzioni.D: The project uses feature sprints, Kanban boards and retrospectives to manage its work.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Correct. Predictive plans upfront and executes sequentially to a single release: ideal for definable work with well-known risks.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Prototypes with feedback describe iterative.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Smaller features released describe incremental.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. These are tools, not a life cycle.

domande.spiegazione: Predictive for low risk and change.

domande.domanda: You're working as a project manager in an agile team. Which of the following is NOT an example of the execution practices you'll see in agile?

opzioni.A: Testing at all levels, where the team applies end-to-end testing and unit testing.
opzioni.B: Test-driven development, where tests are written first, then the code is written and tested again to see if it passes.
opzioni.C: Spikes: time-boxed research or experiments, useful for estimating, defining acceptance criteria or learning something critical.
opzioni.D: The project management plan, where the project is planned in detail upfront to avoid misunderstandings by stakeholders.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect: this IS an agile execution practice (agile teams prefer automated tests).
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect: this IS an agile execution practice.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect: this IS an agile execution practice.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Correct: this is NOT agile. The project management plan is a key artifact of the predictive (waterfall) approach.

domande.spiegazione: Agile execution practices.

domande.domanda: The product owner has worked with the development team to list all the work to be done, write the user stories for each feature and place them in the product backlog. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Groom the backlog to ensure only important items are worked on.
opzioni.B: Create the schedule management plan.
opzioni.C: Sort the items by business priority, place them in an iteration, complete them and then remove them from the backlog.
opzioni.D: Move the items into the requirements traceability matrix so you can report on their progress.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Kind of OK, but incomplete.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Predictive (waterfall) document.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. Managing requirements via the backlog is a fundamental agile practice: it's the source of truth, continuously reprioritized to deliver maximum value first.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. The RTM can still be used in agile, but it's not the next step.

domande.spiegazione: Manage requirements via backlog.

domande.domanda: The business partner or product owner continuously refines (grooms) the product backlog: adding new stories, reprioritizing stories and removing stories when needed. What role does the development team take during this process?

opzioni.A: Developing the cards as soon as they're added, to ensure maximum value.
opzioni.B: Removing cards from the backlog that don't make sense to complete.
opzioni.C: Estimating the work needed for each card so the product owner can prioritize based on value and effort.
opzioni.D: Coming to daily stand-ups to report on what was done yesterday and what will be done today.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Cards go into the sprint backlog only when prioritized by the product owner.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. That's the product owner's role.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. During grooming the team sizes the work, so the product owner can prioritize by value and time to delivery.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Stand-ups happen, but aren't the team's role in grooming.

domande.spiegazione: Team estimates; PO prioritizes.

domande.domanda: ⚠️ You're working with your agile project team to estimate each task and how long it might take. The team finds it difficult to give an exact figure and worries this might impact project delivery. What can you show them to estimate more accurately? — ⚠️ Note: options/text partly reconstructed from the transcript.

opzioni.A: Estimate by whole iteration, to give a little room for variation.
opzioni.B: Estimate the cards in full days instead of effort per card.
opzioni.C: Use comparative estimates or relative sizing, such as T-shirt sizing or story points.
opzioni.D: Prioritize the backlog based on business value.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Agile estimates the cards, which then roll up into the iteration.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Less accurate: a card may take half a day.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. Relative sizing (story points, often Fibonacci 1-2-3-5-8-13; T-shirt sizes) is easier than predicting exact time; velocity is then measured in the same units.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Not related to estimating.

domande.spiegazione: Velocity uses the same units.
domande.nota: Option D is unclear in the transcript ('Fresno Valley'): reconstructed as business value.
domande.motivo_incertezza: options/text partly reconstructed from the transcript

domande.domanda: You're an agile project manager talking through the iteration with the product owner, who has created the list of items in the product backlog. There's confusion in the team about who should perform story card sizing. What will you tell them?

opzioni.A: The product owner works through the backlog to size the story cards.
opzioni.B: The agile team works together to size the story cards, relying mostly on information from the developers and testers.
opzioni.C: The agile team leader or Scrum Master sizes the story cards for the team.
opzioni.D: The customer sizes the story cards to ensure maximum value.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. It's a team effort.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. Story point sizing is done by the agile team, mainly the developers and testers who will do the work and know best.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Servant leadership means growing the team, not doing the work for it.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. The customer can't know the effort required.

domande.spiegazione: Team sizes stories.

domande.domanda: You've been estimating story cards with your agile project team, but the effort captured has not matched the time the cards actually take to complete. What is the most likely reason?

opzioni.A: The team has not included sick days in the estimate.
opzioni.B: The team has not included testing or refactoring in the estimate.
opzioni.C: The team has not included time to merge the code for continuous integration.
opzioni.D: The team has not included the time it takes for the daily stand-up.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Sick days affect capacity, not the size of a card.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. Card estimates should include all known activities to complete it, including testing, refactoring, complexity and risk.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. CI should be automated and relates to release, not card development.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Not part of estimating a card.

domande.spiegazione: Estimates include all known activities.

domande.domanda: You're an agile team leader talking through the process for your first retrospective, and the team is curious about what they should do. How would a team retrospective normally work?

opzioni.A: Discuss what was successful and what could be improved, and incorporate those into future iterations.
opzioni.B: Discuss what the team liked about working with each other.
opzioni.C: Discuss what went wrong and make sure the team knows who is to blame.
opzioni.D: Discuss the validity of the features being developed.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Correct. A retrospective asks what went well, what could be improved and what still puzzles us, to improve the process.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Partly, but not the purpose.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Blame has no part in agile: the focus is on improving the process.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. That's the product owner's job before iteration planning.

domande.spiegazione: Retrospectives improve process.

domande.domanda: The 12th agile principle is: 'At regular intervals, the team reflects on how to become more effective, then tunes and adjusts its behavior accordingly.' In practice, this is the retrospective. What is the practical reason for including retrospectives in an agile team?

opzioni.A: It reduces the communication time between the project sponsor and the developers.
opzioni.B: It ensures features are released on schedule and on budget.
opzioni.C: It helps the team learn about and improve its process over time.
opzioni.D: It keeps the team focused on the main feature, to deliver the most business value.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. That's more like a stand-up.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Not the purpose.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. Retrospectives use regular, structured feedback to improve the team's process in small increments.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Prioritization is done by the product owner in sprint planning.

domande.spiegazione: Retros drive improvement.

domande.domanda: Retrospectives are typically held at the end of an iteration, but an agile team can hold them at other times too. What is NOT a time when an agile team might hold a retrospective?

opzioni.A: When the team completes or ships something new.
opzioni.B: When more than a few weeks have passed since the previous retrospective.
opzioni.C: When the team appears to be stuck and completed work is not flowing.
opzioni.D: When the feature backlog has not been created and work is yet to begin.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect: this IS a good time.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect: this IS a good time (at least every couple of weeks).
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect: this IS a good time.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Correct: this is NOT a time. There's nothing to gather feedback on before work has started.

domande.spiegazione: Retros reflect on work done.

domande.domanda: You're in a new project team, working out which project life cycle (way of working) to use to deliver the products to your customer, and how far to modify it. What are some of the project factors that will influence your decision to tailor towards agile or other methods?

opzioni.A: Which project life cycle the customer wants to use.
opzioni.B: Which life cycle is the latest, as it must be the best and most interesting to upper management.
opzioni.C: Whether the flow of work is often interrupted by delays or impediments, and whether the work is easily definable or highly uncertain.
opzioni.D: Project approaches should never be tailored.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. The customer tells you what they want delivered, not the life cycle.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Following fads isn't a valid reason.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. Definable vs. high-uncertainty work and interruptions to the flow are key tailoring factors, along with the team's experience.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Approaches should always be tailored: every project is different.

domande.spiegazione: Team experience matters too.

domande.domanda: ⚠️ You're in the forming stages of a new project team and deciding on your way of working. What are some of the factors that will influence how you tailor the project life cycle? — ⚠️ Note: options/text partly reconstructed from the transcript.

opzioni.A: The demand pattern for value or delivery: is it steady or sporadic?
opzioni.B: The rate of process improvement required by the team.
opzioni.C: Whether more than one team is needed to build the product.
opzioni.D: All of the above.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. It's a factor, but not the only one.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. It's a factor, but not the only one.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. It's a factor, but not the only one.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Correct. Almost everything affects the way of working: how the organization works, certain vs. uncertain work, likelihood of change, what has worked before and what the team is comfortable with.

domande.spiegazione: Many factors drive tailoring.
domande.nota: Option D 'All of the above' reconstructed from the commentary.
domande.motivo_incertezza: options/text partly reconstructed from the transcript

domande.domanda: You're working through the backlog with the product owner and estimating the story cards with the development team. The team has never worked on a product like this before and is unsure whether the estimates are accurate enough. What will you recommend they use to get accurate estimates?

opzioni.A: Affinity estimating, using the actual effort from a similar feature on a different project.
opzioni.B: T-shirt sizing, using broad small, medium or large sizes to accommodate variation.
opzioni.C: Three-point estimating, using pessimistic, most likely and optimistic estimates.
opzioni.D: The product owner should estimate the story cards.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Correct. Agile normally estimates bottom-up on small tasks; where that doesn't work, affinity estimating from a similar past feature is the next best choice.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Too broad; usually used at the beginning or for large items.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Not typically used in agile.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. The people doing the work (developers, testers) estimate.

domande.spiegazione: Bottom-up first; affinity next best.

domande.domanda: You're delivering features through your agile project, and the project sponsor and product owner are happy with progress. The sponsor raises a concern about future items and what that development will look like. What will you show them?

opzioni.A: The project management plan.
opzioni.B: The product backlog.
opzioni.C: The product roadmap, showing planned future features and their approximate dates, similar to a Gantt chart.
opzioni.D: The team velocity chart, showing how much the team completes per iteration.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Predictive (waterfall) artifact.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Lists the items, but not when they're coming.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. The product roadmap is a visual display of releases, high level and adjusted as needed, usually created by the product owner.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Useful together with the backlog, but not a view of future features.

domande.spiegazione: Roadmap is like an agile Gantt.

domande.domanda: The agile team is estimating story cards using planning poker for one of the larger features. Some of the team estimated 3 points, while others estimated 8 points. How will you guide them to come to an agreement?

opzioni.A: Ask them to average out the points and assign that value to the card.
opzioni.B: Change the estimating method to accommodate the team decision.
opzioni.C: Change the feature to make it easier to estimate.
opzioni.D: Ask the highest and lowest estimators to explain their reasons, then have the team estimate again until consensus is reached or more information is needed.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Averaging loses the reasons behind the high and low estimates.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. The method isn't the problem.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. The team delivers what the customer wants.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Correct. In planning poker the high and low estimators share their reasons and the team re-estimates until consensus, or decides to gather more information.

domande.spiegazione: Planning poker.

domande.domanda: The agile team is working through a particularly complex feature for which it's difficult to find a solution. As the agile lead, you recommend a spike. What is a spike?

opzioni.A: Shifting the feature into another iteration.
opzioni.B: A time-boxed task to explore or investigate an issue.
opzioni.C: A short meeting at the beginning of the day to discuss tasks in progress.
opzioni.D: A demonstration of the feature to the product owner.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. That's just backlog management.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. A spike is time-boxed research, separate from development work, used only when something needs to be figured out.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. That's the stand-up.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. That's the sprint review/demonstration.

domande.spiegazione: Spikes are time-boxed.

domande.domanda: You've been completing small, usable increments of value as part of your agile team. When reporting back to the project sponsor, the last iteration was described as a 'fast failure'. What does that mean?

opzioni.A: The iteration did not complete all the story cards in the allotted time.
opzioni.B: The project team found a bug before code delivery.
opzioni.C: The proof of concept for that iteration did not have the intended outcome.
opzioni.D: The product backlog was not well groomed to start the next iteration.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Not what fast failure means.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Not what fast failure means.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. That increment wasn't successful: the team learns from it quickly and adjusts its approach.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. A process matter, not related.

domande.spiegazione: Fail fast, learn, adjust.

domande.domanda: The Scaled Agile Framework (SAFe) details practices, roles and activities at the portfolio, program and project levels, and focuses on organizing the enterprise around value streams that provide value to the customer. What is NOT one of the principles of SAFe?

opzioni.A: Take an economic view and apply systems thinking.
opzioni.B: Visualize and limit work in progress, and reduce batch sizes.
opzioni.C: Plan carefully for a large single-feature release.
opzioni.D: Build incrementally with fast, integrated learning cycles.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect: this IS a SAFe principle (systems thinking: a small change affects the whole system).
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect: this IS a SAFe principle.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct: this is NOT a principle. Planning long term for a single release is a predictive way of working.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect: this IS a SAFe principle.

domande.spiegazione: SAFe scales agile principles.

domande.domanda: The Scaled Agile Framework (SAFe) focuses on detailing practices, roles and activities at the portfolio, program and project levels, and organizes the enterprise around value streams. What is NOT one of the SAFe principles?

opzioni.A: Make sure stakeholders know when you did more work than your teammates.
opzioni.B: Apply cadence and synchronize with cross-domain planning.
opzioni.C: Unlock the intrinsic motivation of knowledge workers.
opzioni.D: Decentralize decision making.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Correct: this is NOT a principle. Agile focuses on individuals and interactions and on the team, not on self-promotion.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect: this IS a SAFe principle (similar to a Scrum of Scrums across teams).
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect: this IS a SAFe principle.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect: this IS a SAFe principle.

domande.spiegazione: People and interactions first.

domande.domanda: Your agile project team has been delivering value to the organization in increments for some time. Executives would like to scale the approach across more teams to gain the benefit of this way of working. Which of the following is NOT an agile scaling framework you might use?

opzioni.A: Scrum of Scrums.
opzioni.B: Scaled Agile Framework (SAFe).
opzioni.C: Kanban iteration retrospective.
opzioni.D: Large-Scale Scrum (LeSS).

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect: this IS a scaling framework.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect: this IS a scaling framework.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct: this is NOT a scaling framework (it doesn't exist).
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect: this IS a scaling framework.

domande.spiegazione: Scaling frameworks.

domande.domanda: The organization you're working in has decided to move towards an agile way of working and project life cycle. How would you describe an agile project life cycle?

opzioni.A: It's both iterative and incremental, to refine work items and deliver frequently.
opzioni.B: It's both iterative and predictive.
opzioni.C: It's both fast and furious, designed to deliver the most bang for your buck.
opzioni.D: It's both predictive and incremental.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Correct. Agile combines iterative (gathering feedback) and incremental (delivering smaller usable features of value).
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Predictive plans everything upfront.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Save it for the movies.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Predictive isn't part of agile.

domande.spiegazione: Agile life cycle.

domande.domanda: There are four main project life cycle approaches to managing a project, with variations in between. What is one of the characteristics of an iterative life cycle approach?

opzioni.A: It does not allow feedback.
opzioni.B: It allows feedback on unfinished work to improve and modify that work.
opzioni.C: It focuses on delivery, not feedback.
opzioni.D: It plans the project upfront and delivers in one go.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Iterative is built on feedback.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. It iterates towards success using prototypes and unreleased versions to gather feedback, then releases in one go.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Feedback is central.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. It does deliver in one go, but it adjusts with feedback rather than planning everything upfront.

domande.spiegazione: Iterative life cycle.

domande.domanda: You're working through a sprint planning meeting with your team. The team has sized the cards and prioritized the backlog. What will you do next to determine how much work can be done during this iteration?

opzioni.A: Count up the user stories the product owner wants completed by the end of the iteration.
opzioni.B: Check the team's velocity against the number of points for the story cards you want to complete.
opzioni.C: Ask the Scrum Master to allocate work to each team member in the fairest manner possible.
opzioni.D: Look at what other teams did in their last iteration to get an idea for your team.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. That's what the PO wants, not what the team can complete.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. Velocity (average completed per sprint) compared with the card points tells you how much fits.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Not related.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Every team is different and may measure differently.

domande.spiegazione: Plan to velocity.

domande.domanda: You're an agile project manager working on the next feature for your product. The product owner asks for an estimate of how long the remaining features may take to complete, and you look at the team's velocity chart. Why?

opzioni.A: The team's average velocity across previous iterations is the best predictor of future iterations.
opzioni.B: Velocity ensures the team never works harder than it has to.
opzioni.C: The Scrum Master has the final say over team velocity to ensure the work gets done.
opzioni.D: The velocity chart shows how quickly new items are picked up by the team.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Correct. Average velocity is the best predictor, because previous iterations typically include the tasks and pitfalls the team will meet in future.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. The team can pull extra cards when it finishes.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Velocity is just a measurement of work completed.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. It measures how much work flows through, not pickup speed.

domande.spiegazione: Velocity forecasts.

domande.domanda: You're the agile lead (Scrum Master) for your agile team, and the next iteration is about to begin. What will you do before planning the next iteration?

opzioni.A: Break the features down into user stories.
opzioni.B: Write the story card acceptance criteria within the team.
opzioni.C: Choose which stories the team will work on in the iteration.
opzioni.D: Work with the product owner to prioritize the highest-value items to work on.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Done by the development team, BAs and PO.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Done by business analysts with developers, testers and the PO.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Partial: priority comes first.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Correct. Features should already be broken into cards; now reprioritize them by business value and the team's velocity.

domande.spiegazione: Iteration planning.

domande.domanda: You're in the middle of a sprint with your agile team, moving the project forward with daily stand-up meetings. What is a stand-up meeting?

opzioni.A: A project kickoff meeting.
opzioni.B: A project progress meeting, where you see how the proposed schedule stands up against the actual schedule.
opzioni.C: A very quick meeting, time-boxed to 15 minutes or less, where the team says what it has accomplished and reports any blockers.
opzioni.D: A team training meeting.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Not a kickoff.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. That's predictive schedule tracking.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. Held daily around the Kanban board; above all it surfaces blockers so the team can swarm on them.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Not a training meeting.

domande.spiegazione: Daily stand-up.

domande.domanda: You're the agile project manager on a software project, and the development team has identified a major risk to the delivery of a certain feature. That feature is not scheduled until very late in the project. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Wait until later in the project, as the problem may be fixed by other features going in.
opzioni.B: Ask the developers to find a way to proceed without that feature.
opzioni.C: Plan a spike around the risk to identify a solution, then prioritize that feature earlier in development.
opzioni.D: Remove all other story cards from the current sprint so the team can swarm around the issue and fix it.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Risks become more expensive the longer they wait.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. The feature may still be needed.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. Agile prioritizes risks early; discovery is done with a time-boxed spike card, while the rest of the team keeps delivering value.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. The team should keep delivering value.

domande.spiegazione: Prioritize risk early.

domande.domanda: Your agile project team is using Scrum to manage the work and deliverables for your project. Which of the following is NOT one of the Scrum events or artifacts?

opzioni.A: The product backlog: a prioritized list of planned product items, managed by the product owner, which evolves from sprint to sprint.
opzioni.B: The sprint backlog: the items that go into the actual sprint.
opzioni.C: Increments or features: product backlog items completed during a sprint, each a step towards the main vision.
opzioni.D: The team area: where the co-located team sits for fast collaboration.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect: this IS a Scrum artifact.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect: this IS a Scrum artifact.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect: this IS a Scrum artifact.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Correct: this is NOT a Scrum event or artifact. Co-location is recommended in agile, but it isn't part of Scrum itself. Read the question carefully!

domande.spiegazione: Read the question carefully.

domande.domanda: Your agile team has been working with Scrum for some time and has become quite familiar with its events and ceremonies. You're asked to explain them to other stakeholders in the organization. What is NOT an example of a Scrum event or ceremony?

opzioni.A: Sprint planning, where the highest-priority items are selected to go into the sprint.
opzioni.B: The daily scrum (stand-up), where the team meets to talk about its tasks.
opzioni.C: The sprint review, where a working piece of software delivered during the sprint is demonstrated.
opzioni.D: The change control board, where all proposed changes are reviewed before being added to the backlog.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect: this IS a Scrum event.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect: this IS a Scrum event.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect: this IS a Scrum event.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Correct: this is NOT a Scrum event. The change control board belongs to predictive (waterfall) life cycles.

domande.spiegazione: Scrum events.

domande.domanda: Scrum is a single-team framework for managing product development, with certain events, ceremonies, roles and responsibilities. Which of the following is NOT a role or responsibility in a Scrum team?

opzioni.A: Product owner.
opzioni.B: Development team.
opzioni.C: Scrum Master.
opzioni.D: Risk manager.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect: this IS a Scrum role (prioritizes the backlog).
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect: this IS a Scrum role (develops the stories and features).
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect: this IS a Scrum role (facilitates the ceremonies).
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Correct: this is NOT a Scrum role. In agile, risk and quality are the whole team's responsibility.

domande.spiegazione: Scrum roles.

domande.domanda: Agile servant leadership is one of the key foundations of an agile team, where leadership, team participation and openness are encouraged. Which of the following is NOT one of the characteristics of a servant leader?

opzioni.A: Promoting self-awareness and helping people grow.
opzioni.B: Listening to others more than speaking yourself.
opzioni.C: Serving those on the team by removing blockers.
opzioni.D: Reporting on low performers to ensure the team is streamlined.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect: this IS a characteristic.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect: this IS a characteristic.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect: this IS a characteristic.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Correct: this is NOT a characteristic. Servant leadership builds psychological safety, openness and growth.

domande.spiegazione: Servant leadership builds safety.

domande.domanda: Your team is about to develop a new product for your organization. Depending on the product, stakeholders, risk appetite, need for value and more, the life cycle (way of working) will change. Which of the following represents an incremental life cycle approach?

opzioni.A: It provides unfinished deliverables.
opzioni.B: It provides value in one release.
opzioni.C: It provides multiple finished deliverables that the customer can use immediately.
opzioni.D: It provides a way for the team to do less with more, by releasing only a small feature.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Increments must be finished, usable parts.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Incremental has multiple releases.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. Small increments the customer can use immediately, gain value from and give feedback on.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Not the definition.

domande.spiegazione: Incremental life cycle.

domande.domanda: You're working with your agile team to size story cards and place them in upcoming iterations. You notice that the points allocated to the story cards are getting bigger and bigger with each release. Why might this be happening?

opzioni.A: The product owner keeps adding scope to the project.
opzioni.B: Technical debt is being built on from previous releases.
opzioni.C: Team members are not working their full allotted hours.
opzioni.D: Team members are working too hard and burning out.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Added scope is handled by prioritization; it doesn't make cards bigger.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. Code rushed to production without refactoring creates more and more work in each release. Regular refactoring and slack cards help.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Hours don't change the story points.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Burnout matters, but it doesn't change the story points.

domande.spiegazione: Refactor regularly; build in slack.

domande.domanda: The project sponsor of your agile team is quite familiar with Lean and agile terms and methods. She asks you for the average cycle time and the average lead time for the project so far. What will you give her?

opzioni.A: The average time for team leave and team attendance.
opzioni.B: The time to complete stand-ups and the time to complete retrospectives.
opzioni.C: The average time to complete story cards and the time to complete features.
opzioni.D: The average team downtime and the average time to complete releases.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Cycle and lead time are about the work.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Not cycle or lead time.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. Cycle time measures shorter tasks (story cards); lead time measures a whole feature from beginning to end.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Not cycle or lead time.

domande.spiegazione: Lean terms.

domande.domanda: You're reviewing the velocity of your agile team and notice it has increased over the past two iterations. What might be the reason?

opzioni.A: The productivity of one team member has increased.
opzioni.B: The team no longer tests each card.
opzioni.C: The team estimated the story cards more accurately.
opzioni.D: The product owner removed some features from the backlog.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Correct. Velocity is the work completed by the whole team, so one person's higher productivity lifts the team's velocity.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Every card should still be tested.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Not directly related to velocity increasing.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Removing backlog items doesn't change how much is completed per sprint.

domande.spiegazione: Velocity vs throughput.

domande.domanda: You're an agile project manager talking through the defects raised so far with your team. To get a more accurate view of effort per card, you ask the quality tester to begin tracking defect cycle time. What will they report back on?

opzioni.A: How many defects were discovered.
opzioni.B: How long it took to fix a defect, from the time it was found to the time it was fixed.
opzioni.C: How many cycles it takes to raise a defect.
opzioni.D: The number of features in the backlog that have experienced defects.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. That's a count, not a time.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. Cycle time measures a smaller item from start to finish: usually a story card, but also a defect.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Not meaningful.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. That's a count.

domande.spiegazione: Cycle time applies to defects.

domande.domanda: You're checking in with the quality tester in your agile team, who tells you there are a number of escaped defects in the most recently completed feature. What are they referring to?

opzioni.A: A feature that was not completed by the end of the iteration.
opzioni.B: Code that needs to be refactored.
opzioni.C: Defects that have made it through testing and quality assurance.
opzioni.D: Team members who did not attend the daily stand-up.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Not about defects.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. That's refactoring.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. Escaped defects get past testing and release into the customer's hands: the most expensive kind to fix.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Not about defects.

domande.spiegazione: Escaped defects.

domande.domanda: Agile approaches emphasize servant leadership to empower teams: leading through service to the team, understanding and addressing the needs and development of team members to enable the highest possible performance. In what order do servant leaders approach project work?

opzioni.A: Purpose, people and process.
opzioni.B: People, systems and technology.
opzioni.C: Information, reporting and process.
opzioni.D: Plant, people and machine.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Correct. Start with why (purpose), then grow and develop the people, then ensure a solid process for the day-to-day work.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Servant leadership is more about growing people.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Not the order.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Not the order.

domande.spiegazione: Servant leadership order.

domande.domanda: You've been part of an agile team for some time and are working on aspects of servant leadership to improve the results in your team. What is NOT one of the characteristics of a servant leader?

opzioni.A: Coaching versus controlling.
opzioni.B: Promoting safety.
opzioni.C: Promoting the energy and intelligence of others.
opzioni.D: Ensuring the team does what you say.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect: this IS a characteristic.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect: this IS a characteristic (psychological safety).
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect: this IS a characteristic.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Correct: this is NOT a characteristic. The servant leader facilitates; the team are the experts. No directive leadership.

domande.spiegazione: Servant leadership.

domande.domanda: You've delivered half of the features in the backlog of your agile project, and you notice quite a difference in the number of defects over the last three iterations. You ask the team to investigate both common cause and special cause variation. What will they investigate?

opzioni.A: Issues that arose from normal operations and issues that arose from a unique or new condition.
opzioni.B: Issues caused by the common area and issues caused by the special software.
opzioni.C: Issues found in the last release and issues found in this release.
opzioni.D: Issues caused by continuous integration and issues caused by no integration.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Correct. In Lean (Toyota Production System), common cause = normal operations; special cause = special or new factors.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Wordplay trap.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Not the meaning.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Not the meaning.

domande.spiegazione: Lean concept.

domande.domanda: You've built an experienced agile team that has delivered consistently for your organization.
